nahhas-meani:1-1.t:
Among that is His saying, the Exalted: ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ أَوْفُواْ بِٱلْعُقُودِ﴾.
Mujāhid said: العقودُ (contracts) are the covenants (العهود).
And that is well known in the language; one says: "عهدتُ إليه" when I commanded him with something, and "عقدتُ عليه" and "عاقدتُه" when I commanded him and took a firm pledge from him.
And it was said: By العقود here the obligatory duties (farāʾiḍ) are meant.
* Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿أُحِلَّتْ لَكُمْ بَهِيمَةُ ٱلأَنْعَامِ إِلاَّ مَا يُتْلَىٰ عَلَيْكُمْ﴾.
Al-Ḥasan said: الأنعامُ are camels, cattle and sheep/goats.
And ʿAwf narrated from al-Ḥasan: ﴿بَهِيمَةُ ٱلأَنْعَامِ﴾: the sheep, the camel and the cow.
And Zuhayr ibn Muʿāwiya narrated from Qābūs ibn Abī Ẓabyān, who said: "We slaughtered a cow, and the boys took from its belly a large foetus that had already grown hair; they roasted it and then brought it to Abū Ẓabyān, who said: ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās told us that this is بهيمة الأنعام."
Abū Jaʿfar said: The first is more fitting, because after it comes ﴿إِلاَّ مَا يُتْلَىٰ عَلَيْكُمْ﴾, and among foetuses there is nothing to be excepted.
And they were called "بهيمة الأنعام" because they are closed off (ubhimat) from discernment.
* Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿غَيْرَ مُحِلِّي ٱلصَّيْدِ وَأَنْتُمْ حُرُمٌ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَحْكُمُ مَا يُرِيدُ﴾.
The singular of الحُرُم is حرام, and حرام is in the sense of محرم (one in the state of iḥrām); he is called محرم and حرام because marriage and other things have been made forbidden to him.
One says: أحرمَ when he enters the Sanctuary (al-ḥaram), just as one says أَشْتَى when he enters winter, and أَشْهَر when he enters the month.

nahhas-meani:2-2.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ لاَ تُحِلُّواْ شَعَآئِرَ ٱللَّهِ﴾.
Abū ʿUbayda said: الشعائرُ are the sacrificial offerings (al-hadāyā); the singular is شَعِيرة.
Someone else said: شعيرة is in the sense of مُشْعَرة (marked).
Al-Aṣmaʿī said: أشعرتُها means: I marked it.
And al-Aswad ibn Yazīd narrated from ʿĀʾisha that she said: It is only marked so that it may be known to be a sacrificial camel (badana).
Mujāhid said: "The rites (shaʿāʾir) of Allah" are al-Ṣafā, al-Marwa and the Sanctuary.
And the meaning according to this view is: Do not make hunting lawful in the Sanctuary; and the implied construction (taqdīr) is: Do not make the rites of Allah lawful for yourselves.
And whoever says that they are the sacrificial camels (al-budn), for him the verse is abrogated.
Al-Shaʿbī said: There is no abrogated verse in al-Māʾida except ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ لاَ تُحِلُّواْ شَعَآئِرَ ٱللَّهِ﴾; and Qatāda said likewise. [Translator's note: the text reads «ليس في المائدة آية منسوخة» without an explicit «إلا» (except); the sense of exception is implied by what follows and is rendered accordingly.]
And he said: It was abrogated by ﴿فَاقْتلُوا المُشْرِكينَ حَيْثُ وَجَدْتُموهُمْ﴾; before that they had been prevented from fighting them in the (sacred) month when they were heading for the Sacred House.
* Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿وَلاَ ٱلشَّهْرَ ٱلْحَرَامَ﴾, and it is Rajab.
* Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿وَلاَ ٱلْهَدْيَ﴾; the singular of الهَدْي is هَدْيَة.
* Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿وَلاَ ٱلْقَلاۤئِدَ﴾.
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk and ʿAṭāʾ said: They used to take (something) from the trees of the Sanctuary, and they would not be approached (with harm) when it was seen on them.
* Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿وَلاۤ آمِّينَ ٱلْبَيْتَ ٱلْحَرَامَ﴾. الأَمُّ is intending (al-qaṣd), i.e. do not deem it lawful to obstruct those heading for the Sacred House.
And it is possible that the meaning is: Do not violate the intent of those heading (there), and then (the muḍāf) was omitted.
* Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿يَبْتَغُونَ فَضْلاً مِّن رَّبِّهِمْ وَرِضْوَاناً﴾.
Warqāʾ said, from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid: They seek reward and trade.
* Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿وَإِذَا حَلَلْتُمْ فَٱصْطَادُواْ﴾.
And this is a permission after a prohibition, and not an obligation.
* Then He, the Exalted, said: ﴿وَلاَ يَجْرِمَنَّكُمْ شَنَآنُ قَوْمٍ أَن صَدُّوكُمْ عَنِ ٱلْمَسْجِدِ ٱلْحَرَامِ أَن تَعْتَدُواْ﴾.
Abū ʿUbayda said: ﴿وَلاَ يَجْرِمَنَّكُمْ﴾ means: let it not earn you; and he recited:
وَلَقَدْ طَعَنْتُ أَبَا عُيَيْنَةَ طَعْنَةً * جَرمَتْ فَزَارةُ بَعْدَهَا أَنْ يَغْضَبُوا
(I struck Abū ʿUyayna a thrust after which it was earned for Fazāra that they should be angry.)
Al-Akhfash said: And let it not make it your due (lā yuḥaqqinnakum).
Al-Farrāʾ said: And let it not drive you.
And these meanings are close to one another, because whoever drives a man to hate another man has earned him that hatred; and since the matter is so, what is best to say is what Ibn ʿAbbās and Qatāda said; they said: That is, let not the hatred of a people drive you to aggression.
And al-Aʿmash read ﴿وَلاَ يُجْرِمَنَّكُمْ﴾ with a ḍamma on the yāʾ.
Al-Kisāʾī said: جَرَمَ يَجْرِمُ and أجرم يُجْرِمُ have one meaning; the fatḥa (form) is more common in this sense, and the ḍamma (form) is more common in the sense of committing a crime.
And الشَّنَآنُ is hatred; and it is read "شَنْئَانُ" with a sukūn on the nūn, and that is not good, because maṣdars (verbal nouns) do not come on the pattern "فَعْلاَن".
And Abū ʿAmr read (إِنْ صَدُّوكُمْ) with a kasra on the hamza, in the sense of a condition.
And it is narrated from al-Aʿmash that he read (إِنْ يصُدّوكُمْ).
And that is a solecism (laḥn) according to the grammarians, because when "إن" makes the verb jussive (majzūm), its apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) does not precede it. And the meaning according to the reading of those who read with a fatḥa is: ﴿ولا يجرمنكم شَنَآنُ قَوْم﴾ because they barred you from the Sacred Mosque, (to the point) that you transgress.
And whoever reads with a kasra, the meaning for him is: if they do this.
And the meaning is according to the fatḥa, because it is narrated (that when the Prophet ﷺ conquered Mecca, a man from among his Companions killed a man from the people of Mecca who used to kill the allies of the Prophet ﷺ, and this verse was revealed).

nahhas-meani:3-3.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿حُرِّمَتْ عَلَيْكُمُ ٱلْمَيْتَةُ وَٱلْدَّمُ وَلَحْمُ ٱلْخِنْزِيرِ﴾.
One says مَيْتَةٌ and مَيِّيَةٌ with one meaning; this is the view of the trustworthy among the lexicographers. [Translator's note: «مَيِّيَةٌ» is as written; the expected form is «مَيِّتَةٌ».]
And it was said: الميِّتَةُ is that which has not yet died, and المْيتَة is that which has already died.
And it is narrated that they used to put blood in intestines, then roast them and eat them; so Allah, Majestic and Mighty, forbade blood that is poured out (al-masfūḥ), which is that which is shed.
* Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿وَمَآ أُهِلَّ لِغَيْرِ ٱللَّهِ بِهِ﴾.
That is, what was slaughtered for other than Allah, with a name other than His mentioned over it.
And the basic sense of al-ihlāl is the voice; from it is the term al-ihlāl for the Hajj, which is raising the voice with the talbiya and the binding undertaking of the Hajj; from it is istihlāl of the newborn (its first cry); and from it is "أهلَّ الهلالُ" (the new moon appeared), because when people saw it they pointed to it with their voices.
* Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿وَٱلْمُنْخَنِقَةُ﴾.
Qatāda said: It is the one that dies in its strangling.
* Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿وَٱلْمَوْقُوذَةُ﴾.
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: They used to take a sheep or another of the livestock and beat it in front of their gods until it died, then eat it.
And one says: وَقَذَهُ and أَقَذَهُ, so it is مَوْقَوْذ and مُوقَذ, when he beat it until it was on the brink of death; and from this one says: "So-and-so is وقيذ (gravely stricken)."
* Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿وَٱلْمُتَرَدِّيَةُ﴾.
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: المتردية is (the animal) that falls into a well or from a mountain; one says تردى when it falls; and from it is ﴿وَمَا يُغْني عَنْهُ مَالُهُ إِذَا تَرَدَّى﴾.
And النطيحة is the one that has been gored.
* Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿وَمَآ أَكَلَ ٱلسَّبُعُ﴾.
That is, what it preyed upon and ate part of.
And al-Ḥasan read: السَّبْعُ, with a sukūn, because the ḍamma is felt to be heavy.
* Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿إِلاَّ مَا ذَكَّيْتُمْ﴾.
And al-tadhkiya (ritual slaughter) is that the jugular veins gush with blood and it convulses as the slaughtered animal convulses.
And the basic sense of al-tadhkiya in the language is completeness; Zuhayr said:
يُفضِّلُهُ إذَا اجتَهَدَا عَلَيهِ * تَمَامُ السِنِّ منهُ والذَّكَاءُ
(When the two strive against him, his full age and his maturity give him the advantage.)
And from it: "So-and-so has ذكاء," i.e. he is complete in understanding; and "ذكيتُ النار," i.e. I completed its kindling.
And "ذكَّيْتُ الذبيحة": I completed its slaughter as it ought to be done.
* Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿وَمَا ذُبِحَ عَلَى ٱلنُّصُبِ﴾.
And Ṭalḥa read (عَلَى النُّصْبِ).
Mujāhid said: They were stones around Mecca on which they used to slaughter, and sometimes they would replace them.
And it is possible that it is the plural of niṣāb.
* Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿وَأَنْ تَسْتَقْسِمُواْ بِٱلأَزْلاَمِ﴾.
Qatāda said: When one of them wanted to set out, he would write on a qidḥ — meaning an arrow — "Command me to set out," and on another "Do not command me to set out," and he would put between them a blank arrow (manīḥ) with nothing written on it; then he would shuffle them: if the one with "Command me to set out" came out, he set out; if the one with "Do not command me to set out" came out, he did not set out; and if the blank one came out, he went back and shuffled them again.
And this act was only called istiqsām because they sought by it to have their portion (of provision) and what they wanted allotted, just as one says istisqāʾ for asking for water.
And the counterpart of this which Allah has forbidden is the astrologer's saying: "Do not set out because of such-and-such a star," or "Set out because of such-and-such a star."
And He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿وَمَا تَدْرِي نَفْسٌ مَاذَا تَكْسِبُ غَداً وَمَا تَدْرِي نَفْسٌ بِأَيِّ أَرْضٍ تَمُوتُ﴾.
Abū Jaʿfar said: Muḥammad ibn Jarīr mentioned that Ibn Wakīʿ narrated to them from his father, from Sharīk, from Abū Ḥuṣayn, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, that al-azlām were white pebbles which they used to cast.
Muḥammad ibn Jarīr said: Sufyān ibn Wakīʿ said to us: It is chess.
* Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿ذَٰلِكُمْ فِسْقٌ﴾.
And al-fisq is going out, i.e. going out from the lawful into the forbidden.
* And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿ٱلْيَوْمَ يَئِسَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ مِن دِينِكُمْ﴾.
Ibn ʿAbbās said: ﴿يَئِسَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ مِن دِينِكُمْ﴾.
The meaning: Those who disbelieved have despaired of the Jāhiliyya returning.
And Warqāʾ said: The meaning is: Now those who disbelieved have despaired of your religion.
And this is well known among the lexicographers, as you say: "Today I have grown too old for this."
* And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿ٱلْيَوْمَ أَكْمَلْتُ لَكُمْ دِينَكُمْ﴾.
It is narrated that some people of the Jews said: "Had this verse been revealed to us, we would have taken that day as a festival." So ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "It was revealed on a Friday, the Day of ʿArafa."
And concerning the meaning of the verse there are two views:
One of them: Now I have perfected your religion for you by destroying your enemy and making your religion prevail over all religion; just as you say "What we wanted has been completed for us," when you have been spared your enemy.
And it is possible that the meaning is: Today I have perfected your religion for you, beyond what you need of the lawful and the forbidden in the matter of your religion.
And Isrāʾīl narrated from Abū Isḥāq from Abū Maysara that he said: In al-Māʾida there are eighteen obligations that are not in any other (surah): "the prohibition of carrion, blood, the flesh of swine, what has been dedicated to other than Allah, the strangled, the beaten to death, the one killed by a fall, the gored, what a beast of prey has eaten, what has been slaughtered on stone altars, and seeking to know one's lot by divining arrows; the making lawful of the food of those who were given (the Book), and the chaste women of those who were given the Book; trained hunting animals (al-jawāriḥ mukallibīn); the completion of purification: ﴿إذا قُمْتُم إِلى الصَّلاَةِ فَاْغسِلُوا وُجُوهَكُمْ﴾; and His saying, the Exalted: ﴿والسَّارِقُ والسَّارِقَةُ فَاقْطَعُوا أَيْدِيَهُمَا﴾; and His saying, the Exalted: ﴿مَا جَعَلَ اللَّهُ مِنْ بَحِيرَةٍ، وَلا سَائِبَةٍ، وَلاَ وَصِيلَةٍ، وَلاَ حَامٍ﴾."
And it is narrated that it was the last surah revealed.
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿فَمَنِ ٱضْطُرَّ فِي مَخْمَصَةٍ﴾.
المخمصة is the shrinking of the belly from hunger.
* Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿غَيْرَ مُتَجَانِفٍ لإِثْمٍ﴾.
Qatāda said: The sin here is that you eat of it beyond satiety.
* Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ غَفُورٌ رَّحِيمٌ﴾.
That is, He had mercy on you and made these things permissible for you in necessity.

nahhas-meani:4-4.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿يَسْأَلُونَكَ مَاذَآ أُحِلَّ لَهُمْ قُلْ أُحِلَّ لَكُمُ ٱلطَّيِّبَاتُ وَمَا عَلَّمْتُمْ مِّنَ ٱلْجَوَارِحِ مُكَلِّبِينَ﴾.
And ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, al-Ḥasan and Abū Razīn read ﴿مُكْلِبِين﴾.
And the meaning of مكَلِّبِينَ is: owners of dogs; one says كَلَّبَ, so he is مكَلِّب and كَلاَّب; and one says أَكْلَب, so he is مَكْلِب, when he has many dogs, just as one says أمشى, so he is ممش, when his livestock become many.
And al-Aṣmaʿī recited:
وكلُّ فتى وإنْ أَمْشَى فَأَثْرَى * سَتَخْلِجُهُ عنِ الدُّنْيَا مَنُونُ
(Every young man, even if his flocks multiply and he grows rich, will be snatched from this world by fate.)
And it is narrated from Abū Rāfiʿ that he said: When the Prophet ﷺ ordered the killing of dogs, they asked him: What is lawful of this kind (umma) that you have ordered to be killed? So there was revealed ﴿يَسْأَلُونَكَ مَاذَآ أُحِلَّ لَهُمْ﴾, and he recited to the end of the verse.
And al-jawāriḥ in the language are the earners; one says: "So-and-so (fem.) has no jāriḥ," i.e. no earner.
And Mujāhid said concerning the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿وَيَعْلَمُ مَا جَرَحْتُم بِالنَّهَارِ﴾; he said: what you have earned.
And Mujāhid said concerning the meaning of ﴿ٱلْجَوَارِحِ﴾ that they are dogs and birds.
And Ṭāwūs said: Hunting by birds is lawful, because of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿مُكَلِّبِينَ﴾. [Translator's note: as written; the argument from ﴿مُكَلِّبِينَ﴾ and the following sentences suggest that Ṭāwūs's reported view was that hunting by birds is not lawful.]
And there is no evidence in the verse for the prohibition of hunting by anything other than dogs, because the meaning of "مكلِّبينَ" is "those who set (animals) on (the game)."
And the consensus strengthens Ṭāwūs's view on the lawfulness of hunting by birds.
* And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿فَكُلُواْ مِمَّآ أَمْسَكْنَ عَلَيْكُمْ﴾.
Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ, Salmān, ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar and Abū Hurayra said: "If it holds (the game) for you, then eat, even if it has eaten (from it)"; and this is the view of the people of Medina.
And it is narrated from ʿAdī ibn Ḥātim from the Prophet ﷺ that he said: "If it holds it for you and has not eaten, then eat"; and this is the view of the people of Kufa. [Translator's note: the text repeats «عليك» («for you») twice; translated once.]

nahhas-meani:96-96.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أُحِلَّ لَكُمْ صَيْدُ ٱلْبَحْرِ وَطَعَامُهُ مَتَاعاً لَّكُمْ وَلِلسَّيَّارَةِ﴾.
ʿUmar ibn Abī Salama related [from his father] from Abū Hurayra from ʿUmar, who said:
"صيدُ البحرِ (the game of the sea) is what is caught from it, and طعامُه (its food) is what it casts up."
Ibn ʿAbbās likewise related it via Saʿīd ibn Jubayr. [Translator's note: the source gives no wording after the colon here.]
It has also been said: طعامُه is what is sown, because it grows by means of it (i.e. the water).
Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said: طعامُه is the salted (fish) from it, and صيدُه is what is fresh.
What is evident is that صيده means that you hunt, and طعامه means that you eat the game.
Mujāhid said: ﴿لَّكُمْ﴾ "for you" means for the people of the villages, and ﴿وَلِلسَّيَّارَةِ﴾ "and for the travellers" means for the people of the cities.
It has also been said: السيَّارة are the travellers, and this is the more appropriate view.

nahhas-meani:97-97.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿جَعَلَ ٱللَّهُ ٱلْكَعْبَةَ ٱلْبَيْتَ ٱلْحَرَامَ قِيَاماً لِّلنَّاسِ﴾.
There are two views on it:
One of them — and it is closer to the meaning — is that they are sustained by it and are safe.
Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said: (قِيَاماً means) a strengthening for the religion.
The other view is that they uphold its rites.
As for His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He, after this: ﴿ذٰلِكَ لِتَعْلَمُوۤاْ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَعْلَمُ مَا فِي ٱلسَّمَاوَاتِ وَمَا فِي ٱلأَرْضِ﴾ and how it corresponds to the first part, Abū al-ʿAbbās Muḥammad ibn Yazīd [Translator's note: i.e. al-Mubarrad] said: In the Jāhiliyya they used to venerate the Sacred House and the sacred months, to the point that they used to call Rajab — which is one of the sacred months — "al-Aṣamm" (the Deaf), because the clash of weapons was not heard in it. Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, knew what would come from them in the way of raiding one another, so He inspired them not to fight in the sacred months, nor at the Sacred House, nor (to attack) anyone who had the garlands (القلائد) with him. So the One who inspired them with this knows what is in the heavens and what is in the earth.
Abū Isḥāq [Translator's note: i.e. al-Zajjāj] said: Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He, informed the Prophet ﷺ in this sura of things that the hypocrites and the Jews kept secret, saying, Majestic and Mighty is He:
﴿سمَّاعُون للكَذِبِ سَمَّاعُونَ لِقَوْمٍ آخَرِينَ لَمْ يَأْتُوكَ﴾.
and (He informed him of) the matter of the two adulterers; and His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He, about that, ﴿لِتَعْلَمُوۤاْ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَعْلَمُ مَا فِي ٱلسَّمَاوَاتِ وَمَا فِي ٱلأَرْضِ﴾, is connected to these things, i.e. the One who informed you of them knows what is in the heavens and what is in the earth.
The proof of the soundness of this view is His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿مَا عَلَى الرَّسُولِ إِلاَّ البَلاَغُ وَاللَّهُ يَعلمُ مَا تُبْدُون وَمَا كُنْتُمْ تَكْتُمُونَ﴾.

nahhas-meani:101-101.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يٰأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ لاَ تَسْأَلُواْ عَنْ أَشْيَآءَ إِن تُبْدَ لَكُمْ﴾.
The meaning of ﴿إِن تُبْدَ لَكُمْ﴾ is: if they are made manifest.
Shuʿba said: Mūsā ibn Anas informed me from Anas ibn Mālik that a man said to the Prophet ﷺ: "O Messenger of Allah, who is my father?" He said: "Your father is so-and-so." So Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He, revealed ﴿يٰأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ لاَ تَسْأَلُواْ عَنْ أَشْيَآءَ إِن تُبْدَ لَكُمْ تَسُؤْكُمْ﴾.
Ibrāhīm al-Hajarī related from Abū ʿIyāḍ from Abū Hurayra that a man said: "O Messenger of Allah, has the Hajj been made obligatory every year?" He said: "Had I said it (i.e. yes), it would have become obligatory, and had it become obligatory and you abandoned it, you would have disbelieved."
Abū Ṣāliḥ related from Abū Hurayra, who said: The Prophet ﷺ said: "No person will ask me about anything in this sitting of mine but that I will inform him of it." A man said: "O Messenger of Allah, who is my father?" So he told him, and there was revealed ﴿لاَ تَسْأَلُواْ عَنْ أَشْيَآءَ إِن تُبْدَ لَكُمْ تَسُؤْكُمْ﴾.
And (it was revealed) so that He would not burden them with seeking the realities of things from Him, Majestic and Mighty is He. [Translator's note: the sentence begins abruptly with "and that…", apparently continuing a view not fully stated in the source.]
It has also been said: this was forbidden only because Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He, loved to keep His servants' affairs covered, as a mercy from Him to them, and loved that they should not propose questions (of their own devising).
The Prophet ﷺ said: "Leave me as long as I leave you, for those before you perished only because of their many questions and their disagreeing with their prophets." [Translator's note: the source misspells the eulogy as «صبى الله عليه وسلم».]
ʿAbd al-Karīm related from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, who said: ﴿لاَ تَسْأَلُواْ عَنْ أَشْيَآءَ إِن تُبْدَ لَكُمْ تَسُؤْكُمْ﴾ was revealed concerning those who asked about the baḥīra, the sāʾiba and the waṣīla.
Do you not see that after it comes ﴿مَا جَعَلَ الله مِنْ بَحِيْرةٍ، ولا سَائِبَةٍ، وَلاَ وَصِيلَةٍ وَلاَ حَامٍ﴾?
I say: the best of these views is the second, namely that Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He, loved to keep His servants' affairs covered, and referred their rulings back to the outward (ẓāhir), which is within their capacity.

nahhas-meani:102-102.t:
What shows that this is the correct (view) is His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿قَدْ سَأَلَهَا قَوْمٌ مِّن قَبْلِكُمْ ثُمَّ أَصْبَحُواْ بِهَا كَافِرِينَ﴾.
Miqsam said: (This is) about the signs which the nations asked of their prophets, may Allah bless them and grant them peace, i.e. so they showed them to them, and then their peoples disbelieved in them afterwards.
The people of tafsīr differed about "al-baḥīra, al-sāʾiba, al-waṣīla and al-ḥām".
Abū Jaʿfar said: We will mention of their statements those with which the statement of the philologists (ahl al-lugha) agrees.
It is the meaning of the statement of Ibn ʿAbbās and al-Ḍaḥḥāk: the baḥīra is the she-camel when she has given birth five times and the last of them was a male; they slit her ear and let her go free; she was not kept from any pasture, and no one rode her.
In the narration of Ibn ʿAbbās: they would take the fifth (offspring) and slaughter it, and its meat was for the men and not the women; if it was a female, they let it live and left it to graze with its mother, after slitting the mother's ear and refraining from making use of her; and if it was (born) dead, the men and the women shared in it.
On its derivation there are two views:
One of them is that one says بَحَرَهُ when he has slit it.
The other view is that it is from amplitude in a thing, likened to the sea (al-baḥr).
The sāʾiba is when one of them vows that if he recovers from his illness he will surely set a she-camel free, or something similar; and when he freed a slave and said "sāʾiba", he had no walāʾ (clientage) over him.
In the ḥadīth from the Prophet ﷺ: "I saw ʿAmr ibn Luḥayy dragging his intestines in the Fire, and he was the first to set free the sawāʾib."
The waṣīla is in sheep and goats specifically: when the ewe gave birth seven times, if the seventh was a male they slaughtered it, and its meat was for the men and not the women; and when she gave birth to a female they did not slaughter it, and they said: "She has joined (waṣalat) her brother."
In the narration from Ibn ʿAbbās: they said "She has joined her brother", and none drank of her milk except the males specifically; and if she was (born) dead, the men and the women ate it. And Ibn ʿAbbās recited ﴿وقالُوا ما في بُطُونِ هَذِه الأَنْعَام خَالِصَةٌ لِذُكُورِنا ومُحرَّم على أَزْواجنا﴾ (to the end of) the verse.
The ḥāmī is the male camel when ten offspring have been born to him from his loins; they said: "He has protected (ḥamā) his back", so he was not ridden and was let go free, and he was in the same status as the baḥīra.
In the narration from Ibn ʿAbbās: "It is the male camel when the offspring of his offspring have been ridden; they said: He has protected his back."
So Allah made known that this was a fabrication on their part, and said: ﴿وَلَكِنَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَروُا يَفْتَرُونَ عَلَى اللَّهِ الكَذِبَ، وَأَكْثَرُهُمْ لاَ يَعْقِلُون﴾.
Al-Shaʿbī said: "الَّذِينَ لاَ يَعْقِلُونَ" (those who do not understand) are the followers; and those who fabricated understood that they had fabricated.

nahhas-meani:105-105.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يٰأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ عَلَيْكُمْ أَنْفُسَكُمْ﴾.
That is: keep to yourselves, set yourselves right and deliver yourselves from punishment.
* Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿لاَ يَضُرُّكُمْ مَّن ضَلَّ إِذَا ٱهْتَدَيْتُمْ﴾.
There is no proof in this of a dispensation to abandon commanding the right and forbidding the wrong, for Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, has commanded that. The meaning is only: you will not be taken to account for the disbelief of whoever disbelieves; and this has been made clear in the ḥadīth.
Qays ibn Abī Ḥāzim said: I heard Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq, may Allah be pleased with him, say on the pulpit: "You interpret ﴿يٰأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ عَلَيْكُمْ أَنْفُسَكُمْ لاَ يَضُرُّكُمْ مَّن ضَلَّ إِذَا ٱهْتَدَيْتُمْ﴾ (wrongly), but I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: 'When acts of disobedience are committed among people and then they do not change them, Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He, is about to envelop them all in His punishment.'"
Ibn Masʿūd said concerning this verse: "Say it (i.e. enjoin the right) as long as it is accepted from you; then when it is rejected from you, then look to yourselves."
Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said: It is about the People of the Book.
Mujāhid said: It is about the Jews and the Christians and those like them.
The two of them hold that the meaning is: the disbelief of the People of the Book does not harm you once they have paid the jizya.
And this is the explanation of the ḥadīth of Abū Bakr.
As for the ḥadīth of Ibn Masʿūd, it is based on the interpretation of the verse applying to two times: it is acted upon in certain times at the end of time, as Abū Umayya al-Shaʿbānī said: I said to Abū Thaʿlaba al-Khushanī: "What should I do with this verse: ﴿يٰأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ عَلَيْكُمْ أَنْفُسَكُمْ لاَ يَضُرُّكُمْ مَّن ضَلَّ إِذَا ٱهْتَدَيْتُمْ﴾?"
He said: I asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about it, and he said: "Enjoin one another to the right and forbid the wrong, until, when you see avarice obeyed, desire followed, worldly life preferred, and everyone with an opinion delighted with his own opinion [and you see a matter you have no power over (لا يَدَيْ لكَ به, or: لا يدَلكَ به)], then look to yourself and leave the common people."

nahhas-meani:106-106.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يِا أَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ شَهَادَةُ بَيْنِكُمْ إِذَا حَضَرَ أَحَدَكُمُ ٱلْمَوْتُ﴾.
Al-Aʿraj read: (شَهَادَةٌ بَيْنَكُمْ).
Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān read: (شهادة بَيْنَكُمْ).
Whoever reads (شَهَاَدَةُ بَيْنِكُمْ) and (شَهَادَةٌ بَيْنَكُمْ), the meaning for him is "the testimony of two", then شهادة was omitted and اثنين (two) was put in its place in the i'rab (grammatical inflection). [Translator's note: the source lists (شَهَادَةٌ بَيْنَكُمْ) both here and in the next paragraph; one of the two was presumably meant to be a different reading.]
It is also possible that the meaning is: let it be that two persons testify.
Whoever reads (شَهَادَةٌ بَيْنَكُمْ), for him it is without omission, and the meaning is that two persons testify.
As for His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿ٱثْنَانِ ذَوَا عَدْلٍ مِّنْكُمْ أَوْ آخَرَانِ مِنْ غَيْرِكُمْ﴾.
On this there is great disagreement.
Abū Mūsā al-Ashʿarī and Ibn ʿAbbās said: ﴿ذَوَا عَدْلٍ مِّنْكُمْ﴾ means from the people of your religion.
﴿أَوْ آخَرَانِ مِنْ غَيْرِكُمْ﴾ means from the People of the Book.
Among the Followers (tābiʿūn), those who held this view were: ʿAbīda, Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib, Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, Shurayḥ, Ibn Sīrīn and al-Shaʿbī.
Al-Ḥasan and al-Zuhrī said: (ذَوَا عَدْلٍ مِّنْكُمْ) means from your relatives, because they know your affairs better than others; (أَوْ آخَرَانِ مِنْ غَيْرِكُمْ) means from other than your relatives among the Muslims.
One who argued for this view said: The Muslims have agreed unanimously that the testimony of the People of the Book is not admissible against Muslims in anything other than the bequest, and their consensus settles their disagreement. [Translator's note: so in the source; the argument as stated seems to fit the first view rather than that of al-Ḥasan and al-Zuhrī.]
And He said, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿مِمَّنْ تَرْضَوْنَ مِنَ الشُّهَدَاءِ﴾, which shows that some of them are of those who are not approved; so the disbeliever must, all the more, not be approved. And He said, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿تَحْبِسُونَهُمَا مِن بَعْدِ ٱلصَّلاَةِ﴾ — so how would a disbeliever revere the prayer?
Ibrāhīm al-Nakhaʿī said: The verse is abrogated; it was abrogated by ﴿وأَشْهِدُوا ذَوَيْ عَدْلٍ مِنْكُم﴾.
Zayd ibn Aslam said: That was when the land was (a land of) war and people inherited from one another by bequest. A man died with no one of the people of Islam with him, so this verse was revealed; then the bequest (as a means of inheritance) was abrogated and the fixed shares (farāʾiḍ) were made obligatory.
The meaning of ﴿تَحْبِسُونَهُمَا مِن بَعْدِ ٱلصَّلاَةِ﴾ is: after the afternoon (ʿaṣr) prayer.
The meaning of ﴿لاَ نَشْتَرِي بِهِ ثَمَناً﴾ is: (we will not sell) what we have testified to.
* Then He said, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَلَوْ كَانَ ذَا قُرْبَىٰ﴾.
Its meaning is: even if he is a relative, as He, Glorified is He, said: ﴿وَلَوِ افْتَدَى بِهِ﴾.
* Then He said, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَلاَ نَكْتُمُ شَهَادَةَ ٱللَّهِ إِنَّآ إِذَاً لَّمِنَ ٱلآَثِمِينَ﴾.
ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muslim read (ولا نَكْتُمُ شهادَةً اللهَ), and it admits two meanings:
One of them: the meaning is "and we will not conceal from Allah a testimony".
The other meaning: "and we will not conceal a testimony, by Allah (واللهِ)", then the wāw (of the oath) was omitted and (the name) put in the accusative.
Al-Shaʿbī read (ولا نَكتُمُ شَهَادَةِ اللهِ); this is, in the view of most of the Arabic grammarians, a solecism (laḥn), even though Sībawayh permitted the oath with the genitive.
Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān read ﴿ولا نَكْتُمُ شَهَادَةً اللهِ﴾ as an interrogative. [Translator's note: so in the source; the interrogative reading presumably requires a hamza of interrogation before the divine name (آللهِ), which is not shown.]

nahhas-meani:107-107.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَإِنْ عُثِرَ عَلَىٰ أَنَّهُمَا ٱسْتَحَقَّآ إِثْماً﴾.
Ibrāhīm al-Nakhaʿī said: The meaning is: if it is discovered.
* Then He said, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿فَآخَرَانِ يِقُومَانِ مَقَامَهُمَا مِنَ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱسْتَحَقَّ عَلَيْهِمُ ٱلأَوْلَيَانِ﴾ verse 107].
(That is:) if they are discovered to have committed a betrayal, then two of the heirs of the deceased are commanded (to stand), and they swear and establish their right.
Abū Isḥāq said: This is a difficult passage both in i'rab and in meaning.
Several views have been stated on it, among them:
that the meaning is "from those among whom (فيهم) the two nearest have a right", so (على) stood in place of (في), just as (في) stood in place of (على) in His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿ولأُصَلِبنَّكُمْ في جُذَوعِ النَّخْل﴾.
It has also been said that the meaning is "from those from whom (منهم) the two nearest have a right", and (على) stood in place of (من), as He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿الَّذِينَ إِذَا اكْتَالُوا عَلَى النَّاسِ يَسْتَوفُونَ﴾, i.e. from the people.
He said: The preferred view is that the meaning, in my opinion, is: let the nearest to the deceased stand.
So الأوليانِ is a badal (substitute) for the alif in (يَقُومَانِ), and the meaning is: from those against whom the bequest has become due.
[Ibn ʿAbbās rejected this reading, and read (منَ الذينَ] اسْتَحقَّ عليهم الأَوَّلَيْنِ), and said: "What do you think, if the two nearest were two minors?"

nahhas-meani:109-109.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يَوْمَ يَجْمَعُ ٱللَّهُ ٱلرُّسُلَ فَيَقُولُ مَاذَآ أُجِبْتُمْ﴾? [verse 109].
This question is by way of rebuke to those who denied them.
On the meaning of the verse there are two views:
One of them is that when they were asked they were terrified, and their understanding left them, so they said: "We have no knowledge."
Mujāhid said: When it was said to them "What response did you receive?", they were terrified and said "We have no knowledge"; then, when their minds returned to them, they reported what they knew.
The other view is that the meaning is: we have no knowledge of what was hidden from us.
It has been said: what shows the soundness of this view is ﴿إِنَّكَ أَنتَ عَلاَّمُ ٱلْغُيُوبِ﴾.
This is the position of Ibn Jurayj. [Translator's note: the source spells the name «ابن جُريح».]
Ḥajjāj related from Ibn Jurayj concerning His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يَوْمَ يَجْمَعُ ٱللَّهُ ٱلرُّسُلَ فَيَقُولُ مَاذَآ أُجِبْتُمْ قَالُواْ لاَ عِلْمَ لَنَآ﴾ — he said: It was said to them: "What did you know of the nations after you?"
They said: "We have no knowledge."
Abū ʿUbayd said: This resembles the ḥadīth of the Prophet ﷺ, that he said: "Peoples will come to the Pool and be pulled away, and I will say: 'My community!' and it will be said: 'You do not know what they innovated after you.'"

nahhas-meani:110-110.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إِذْ قَالَ ٱللَّهُ يٰعِيسَى ٱبْنَ مَرْيَمَ ٱذْكُرْ نِعْمَتِي عَلَيْكَ وَعَلَىٰ وَالِدَتِكَ﴾.
His favour upon Maryam is that He, Majestic and Mighty is He, chose her and purified her.
And He said, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿كُلَّمَا دَخَلَ عَلَيْهَا زَكَرِيَّا المِحْرَابَ وَجَدَ عِنْدَها رِزْقَاً﴾.
* And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿إِذْ أَيَّدتُّكَ بِرُوحِ ٱلْقُدُسِ﴾.
أَيَّدتُكَ means: I strengthened you; and رُوحُ القُدُس is Jibrīl ﷺ.
It has been said: He strengthened him with him when they intended to kill him, and strengthened him with him in argument.

nahhas-meani:111-111.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَإِذْ أَوْحَيْتُ إِلَى ٱلْحَوَارِيِّينَ أَنْ آمِنُواْ بِي وَبِرَسُولِي﴾.
It has been said: the meaning of "أوحيتُ" here is "I inspired", as He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿وأَوْحَى ربُّكَ إلى النَّخْلِ﴾.
It has also been said: its meaning is "I commanded", as the poet said:
* وَحَى لَهَا القَرَارَ فَاسْتَقَرَّتِ * (He commanded it to stay still, and it settled.)
It has also been said: the meaning of أوحيتُ here is "I made clear, and I gave guidance through signs and proofs."

nahhas-meani:112-112.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿إِذْ قَالَ ٱلْحَوَارِيُّونَ يٰعِيسَى ٱبْنَ مَرْيَمَ هَلْ يَسْتَطِيعُ رَبُّكَ أَن يُنَزِّلَ عَلَيْنَا مَآئِدَةً مِّنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ﴾? [verse 112].
Shayba ibn Naṣṣāḥ the Qurʾān-reader related from al-Qāsim ibn Muḥammad from ʿĀʾisha that she said:
The disciples knew Allah too well to say ﴿هَلْ يَسْتَطِيعُ رَبُّكَ﴾ (Is your Lord able…?); rather, they said: هل تستطيع رَبَّك؟ (Are you able [to ask] your Lord?)
ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, may Allah be pleased with him, Muʿādh and Ibn ʿAbbās read ﴿هَلْ تَسْتَطِيعُ ربَّكَ﴾, and Saʿīd ibn Jubayr likewise read it so.
Saʿīd said: It is only "Are you able to ask your Lord?" And the implied form (taqdīr) according to the Arabic grammarians, on this reading, is "Are you capable of asking your Lord?", then (the word سؤال) was omitted, as He said: ﴿وَاسْأَلِ القَرْيَةَ﴾.
And ﴿هَلْ يَسْتَطِيعُ رَبُّكَ﴾ is fine without any omission; it is well known in the speech of the Arabs to say: "Is he able to stand?", meaning "Will he do that at my request?", while you know that he is able to do it.
On the disciples' asking for the sending down of the table there are two views:
One of them is that they asked for that in order to gain certainty, as Ibrāhīm, upon him be peace, said: ﴿رَبِّ أَرِنِي كَيْفَ تُحْيِي المَوْتَى﴾.
The other view is that this request of theirs was before they knew that ʿĪsā heals the one born blind and the leper.
As for ʿĪsā's saying to them: ﴿ٱتَّقُواْ ٱللَّهَ إِن كُنْتُم مُّؤْمِنِينَ﴾, it means: do not propose signs (of your own devising), and do not ask for what other nations have not asked for.
Abū ʿUbayda said: "مائدةٌ" is from (the root denoting) food; it is a fāʿila form with the sense of a mafʿūla (i.e. an active-participle pattern with passive meaning), as He, Majestic and Mighty is He, said: ﴿فِي عِيْشَةٍ رَاضِيَة﴾.
Abū Isḥāq said: "مائدة" in my view is from مَادَ يَمِيدُ, when something moves.
ʿĀṣim al-Jaḥdarī read: ﴿تكونُ لَنَا عِيْدَاً لأُِولاَنَا وَأُخْرَانَا﴾.
Al-Aʿmash read: (تَكُنْ لَنَا عِيدَاً).
It has been said that it was sent down, and it has been said that it was not sent down; and the correct thing is to say that it was sent down, because of His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿قَاَل اللَّهُ إنِّي مُنَزِّلُهَا عَلَيْكُمْ﴾.
Qatāda related from Khilās ibn ʿAmr from ʿAmmār ibn Yāsir — and some of them trace it back (marfūʿ) to the Prophet — that he said: "The table was sent down as bread and meat, and they were commanded not to hoard and not to store anything for the morrow; but they acted treacherously, stored it and put it away, so they were transformed into swine."
Al-Qāsim ibn Zakariyyā al-Muṭarriz narrated to us: al-Ḥusayn ibn Qurʿa narrated to us, he said: Ibn Ḥabīb narrated to us from Saʿīd ibn Qatāda from Khilās ibn ʿAmr from ʿAmmār ibn Yāsir, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The table was sent down as bread and meat, and they were commanded not to store and not to put away; but they stored and put away, so they were transformed into apes and swine." [Translator's note: «سعيد بن قتادة» is so in the source; the chain is usually given as Saʿīd from Qatāda (سعيد عن قتادة).]
[And it is related that this was a trial with which Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He, commanded that they be tested.]
ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd said: The people most severely punished are the people of the table, the family of Pharaoh, and the hypocrites.
Al-Ḥasan said: When they were threatened with punishment if they disobeyed, they said: "We have no need of it", so it was not sent down.
Mujāhid said: When it was said to them: ﴿فَمَنْ يكْفُرْ بعدُ مِنْكُم فإني أُعَذِّبهُ عَذاباً لا أعذِّبه أَحَدَاً مِنَ العَالَمِينَ﴾, they declined its being sent down, so it was not sent down.
It has also been said: this punishment is in the Hereafter.

nahhas-meani:116-116.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَإِذْ قَالَ ٱللَّهُ يٰعِيسَى ٱبْنَ مَرْيَمَ أَأَنتَ قُلتَ لِلنَّاسِ ٱتَّخِذُونِي وَأُمِّيَ إِلَـٰهَيْنِ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ قَالَ سُبْحَانَكَ﴾.
On its meaning there are two views:
One of them is that this will be said to him in the Hereafter.
Qatāda said: This will be said to him on the Day of Resurrection. He said: Do you not see that He said: ﴿هَذا يَوْمُ يَنْفَعُ الصَّادِقينَ صِدْقُهم﴾? That can only be the Day of Resurrection.
Al-Suddī said: He said this to him when He raised him up, because he said: ﴿إنْ تُعَذِّبْهُم فإِنَّهُم عبادُكَ، وَإِنْ تغْفِرْ لَهُمْ فإنَّكَ أَنْتَ العَزِيزُ الحَكِيمُ﴾.
So this is only on the basis that they are (still) in this world, i.e. if You forgive them after repentance.
In support of the holder of this view it has been argued that (إذْ) in the speech of the Arabs is for what is past.
The first view is held by most of the exegetes.
As for the argument of the holder of this second view, that (إذْ) is for what is past, it is not compelling, because Allah's informing, Majestic and Mighty is He, of what will be is equivalent to what has been; on this basis it is sound that it refers to the future. And we will mention their statements on ﴿إِنْ تُعذِّبْهُمْ فَإِنَّهُمْ عِبَادُكَ﴾.
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿تَعْلَمُ مَا فِي نَفْسِي وَلاَ أَعْلَمُ مَا فِي نَفْسِكَ﴾.
Abū Isḥāq said: النفس, according to the philologists, has two meanings:
One of them is that part of a thing is meant by it.
The other is that the whole thing is meant by it, as in your saying: "So-and-so killed himself (نفسه)."
So His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He, ﴿تَعْلَمُ مَا فِي نَفْسِي وَلاَ أَعْلَمُ مَا فِي نَفْسِكَ﴾ means: You know my reality and what is with me.
The proof of this is His saying ﴿إِنَّكَ أَنتَ عَلاَّمُ ٱلْغُيُوبِ﴾.
Someone else said: the meaning is: You know what is hidden of me, and I do not know what is hidden of You.

nahhas-meani:117-117.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿فَلَمَّا تَوَفَّيْتَنِي كُنتَ أَنتَ الرَّقِيبَ عَلَيْهِمْ﴾.
Qatāda said: الرقيبُ is the guardian (al-ḥāfiẓ), and so it is according to the philologists.

nahhas-meani:118-118.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿إِن تُعَذِّبْهُمْ فَإِنَّهُمْ عِبَادُكَ وَإِن تَغْفِرْ لَهُمْ فَإِنَّكَ أَنتَ ٱلْعَزِيزُ ٱلْحَكِيمُ﴾.
There are several views on this:
Among the best of them is that this is by way of submission to Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He; he knew that He does not forgive a disbeliever, but he did not know whether they disbelieved afterwards or believed.
Among the proofs of the soundness of this view is that Saʿīd ibn Jubayr related from Ibn ʿAbbās that the Prophet ﷺ said: "People will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection naked, barefoot and uncircumcised" — and he ﷺ recited ﴿كَمَا بَدَأَكُمْ تَعُودُونَ﴾ — "and some of my community will be taken to the right and to the left, and I will say: 'My companions!' and it will be said: 'They did not cease turning back on their heels after you.' So I will say as the righteous servant said: ﴿وَكُنْتُ عَلَيْهِمْ شَهِيدَاً مَا دُمْتُ فِيهِمْ﴾" — and he recited up to His saying ﴿وَإِنْ تَغْفِرْ لَهُمْ فَإِنَّكَ أَنْتَ العَزِيزُ الحَكِيمُ﴾.
Abū Dharr related that the Prophet ﷺ stood one night repeating ﴿إِنْ تُعَذِّبْهُمْ فَإِنِّهُمْ عِبَادُكَ، وَإِنْ تَغْفِرْ لَهُمْ فَإِنَّكَ أَنْتَ العَزِيزُ الحَكِيمُ﴾.
It has also been said: it is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to His saying: ﴿مَا قُلْتُ لَهُمْ إِلاَّ مَا أَمَرْتَنِي بِهِ﴾.
The meaning on this view is: I said nothing in this world but this.
Abū al-ʿAbbās Muḥammad ibn Yazīd said: Forgiveness of disbelief is not meant by this; the meaning is only: and if You forgive them their lying against me and their attributing to me what I did not say.
Abū Isḥāq said: ʿĪsā ﷺ knew that among them were some who believed; so the meaning in my view — and Allah knows best — is: if You punish them for their fabrication and their disbelief, they have deserved that; and if You forgive whoever of them repents after the enormous fabrication and the disbelief — and it was Your right not to accept his repentance after his audacity against You — then You are the Mighty, the Wise.
As for the statement of whoever said that ʿĪsā ﷺ did not know that the disbeliever is not forgiven, it is a statement that is audacious against the Book of Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He, because a report from Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He, is not abrogated.
It has also been said: ʿĪsā ﷺ believed that they had committed acts of disobedience and done after him what he had not commanded them, yet that they were (still) upon the pillar of his religion; so he said ﴿وَإِنْ تَغْفِرْ لَهُمْ﴾, (meaning) the acts of disobedience they committed after me.

nahhas-meani:119-119.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿هَـٰذَا يَوْمُ يَنفَعُ ٱلصَّادِقِينَ صِدْقُهُمْ﴾.
One of the people of speculative reasoning (ahl al-naẓar) was asked about its meaning, and it was said to him: If the disbeliever were truthful and said "I did wrong", that would not benefit him?
The answer to this is that the Day of Resurrection is a day of requital and not a day of deeds; so the meaning is only: this is a day on which (their truthfulness) benefits those who were truthful in this world, and their refraining from fabricating lies against Allah, Majestic is His name, and against His messengers.
It has also been said: their truthfulness in deeds benefits them; and Allah knows best what He intended.

nahhas-meani:120-120.t:
He said: Abū Jaʿfar Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl al-Naḥḥās informed us, he said: Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā narrated to us: "Abū Ḥātim" Rawḥ ibn al-Faraj, the client of the Ḥaḍārima, narrated to us, he said: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad "Abū Bakr al-ʿUmarī" narrated to us, he said: Ibn Abī Fudayk narrated to us, he said: ʿUmar ibn Ṭalḥa ibn ʿAlqama ibn Waqqāṣ narrated to me, from Nāfiʿ Abū Suhayl ibn Mālik, from Anas ibn Mālik, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Sūrat al-Anʿām was sent down accompanied by a procession of angels that filled what lies between the east and the west, with a resounding noise of glorification, and the earth trembling beneath them" — and the Messenger of Allah was saying "Glory be to my Lord, the Mighty" three times.
[Translator's note: this entry is filed under 5:120 but is the opening of the commentary on Sūrat al-Anʿām.]

nahhas-meani:5-5.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَطَعَامُ ٱلَّذِينَ أُوتُواْ ٱلْكِتَابَ حِلٌّ لَّكُمْ﴾.
Mujāhid and Ibrāhīm said: It means the slaughtered animals.
* And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَٱلْمُحْصَنَاتُ مِنَ ٱلْمُؤْمِنَاتِ وَٱلْمُحْصَنَاتُ مِنَ ٱلَّذِينَ أُوتُواْ ٱلْكِتَابَ مِن قَبْلِكُمْ﴾.
It is narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās that he said: المحصنات are the chaste, sensible women.
And al-Shaʿbī said: It is that she guards her private parts and does not commit fornication, and that she washes after major ritual impurity (janāba).
And the reading according to al-Shaʿbī's view is (والمُحْصِناتُ) with a kasra on the ṣād, and al-Kisāʾī read it so.
And المحصَنَة may be the chaste woman, the married woman, or the free woman; and "free woman" is more fitting here, for if the chaste woman were meant, it would not be permissible to marry a woman until her chastity had been ascertained.
And Mujāhid said: المحصنات are free women.
Abū ʿUbayda said: We hold that marrying the slave-women of the People of the Book is not lawful, because of His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿فَمِنْ مَا مَلَكَتْ أيْمَانُكُمْ مِنْ فَتَيَاتِكُمْ المُؤْمِنَاتِ﴾.
And this is the view held by the majority of scholars.
And what indicates that they are free women is His saying, exalted be His praise: ﴿وَمَنْ لَمْ يَسْتَطِعْ مِنْكُم طَوْلاً أَنْ يَنْكحَ المُحْصَناتِ المُؤمِنَاتِ فَمِنْ مَا مَلَكَتْ أَيْمانُكُمْ مِنْ فَتَيَاتِكُمُ المُؤْمِنَاتِ﴾.
Al-Ḥasan, al-Zuhrī, Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd, Ibrāhīm, Makḥūl and Qatāda said:
Marrying the slave-women of the People of the Book is not lawful, because of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿مِنْ فَتَيَاتِكُمُ المُؤْمِنَاتِ﴾.
* And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَمَن يَكْفُرْ بِٱلإِيمَانِ فَقَدْ حَبِطَ عَمَلُهُ﴾.
Mujāhid and ʿAṭāʾ said: That is, and whoever disbelieves in Allah.
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا إِذَا قُمْتُم إِلَى الصَّلاةِ﴾.
The meaning is: when you intend to stand up for the prayer; and there is evidence for this in the speech.
And similar to it is ﴿فَإِذَا قَرَأْتَ القُرآنَ فَاسْتَعِذْ بِاللَّهِ مِنَ الشَّيْطَانِ الرَّجِيم﴾.
The meaning is: and when you intend to recite.

nahhas-meani:6-6.t:
And concerning His saying, the Exalted: ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ إِذَا قُمْتُمْ إِلَى ٱلصَّلاةِ﴾
there are several views:
The first of them: If he performed ablution after ritual impurity (ḥadath), and then the time of prayer came upon him while he was in a state of purity, he is not required to perform ablution; this is what most people hold, and it is soundly established that the Prophet ﷺ prayed five prayers with a single ablution.
And Zayd ibn Aslam said: That is, when you rise from your beds.
The second view: Ablution was obligatory by this verse upon everyone intending to stand up for the prayer; then the Sunna of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ abrogated that.
The third view: Ablution is due upon everyone who stands up for a prescribed prayer, as Shuʿba narrated from Masʿūd ibn ʿAlī, who said: ʿAlī, may Allah be pleased with him, used to perform ablution for every prayer and recite ﴿إِذَا قُمْتُمْ إِلَى ٱلصَّلاةِ فٱغْسِلُواْ وُجُوهَكُمْ وَأَيْدِيَكُمْ﴾.
* Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿فٱغْسِلُواْ وُجُوهَكُمْ وَأَيْدِيَكُمْ إِلَى ٱلْمَرَافِقِ﴾.
One of the lexicographers said: The meaning is "with the elbows," as He said: ﴿مَنْ أَنْصَارِي إِلَى اللَّهِ﴾,
i.e. with Allah.
And this view is mistaken, because the hand (al-yad) according to the Arabs extends from the fingers to the shoulder, and only the washing of part of it has been prescribed; if "إلى" meant "مع" (with), washing the whole arm would be obligatory and there would be no need to mention the elbows.
And al-mirfaq — one also says al-marfiq — is what lies beyond the hands, on which one leans (yurtafaqu), i.e. reclines.
And the meaning of "إلى" here is the limit (ghāya); it is in its basic usage. However, Abū al-ʿAbbās said: If the second is (part) of the first, then what comes after "إلى" is included in what precedes it, as in His saying, the Exalted: ﴿إِلَى ٱلْمَرَافِقِ﴾,
so the elbows are included in the washing; and if what follows it is not (part) of the first, it is not included in it, as in ﴿ثُمَّ أَتِمُّوا الصِّيَامَ إِلَى الَّلْيلِ﴾.
And someone else said: What comes after "إلى" is not included in what precedes it, except that the elbows are washed by way of following (the Prophet's practice).
* Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿وَٱمْسَحُواْ بِرُؤُوسِكُمْ وَأَرْجُلَكُمْ إِلَى ٱلْكَعْبَينِ﴾.
And the meaning is: "So wash your faces, your hands and your feet," by way of placing earlier and later (taqdīm wa-taʾkhīr).
And whoever reads (وَأَرْجُلِكُم), concerning his reading there are several views:
The first of them: that wiping and washing are one, as Abū Zayd said.
And from it is their saying "تمسَّحْتُ للصلاة" (I wiped myself for the prayer); and the implied construction (taqdīr) is "and your feet by washing."
And what indicates this is His saying ﴿إِلَى ٱلْكَعْبَينِ﴾, for He set a limit to them just as He said of the hands ﴿إِلَى ٱلْمَرَافِقِ﴾.
And what indicates it is the ḥadīth of the Prophet ﷺ: "Woe to the heels from the Fire!"
For if wiping were sufficient, it would be permissible to wipe part (of the foot).
And it is narrated from al-Shaʿbī that he said: (Gabriel, upon him be peace, brought down wiping, and washing) is Sunna.
And the third view is narrated from ʿAlī, may Allah be pleased with him: that he permitted wiping.
Abū Jaʿfar said: However, ʿĀṣim ibn Kulayb narrated from Ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, who said: al-Ḥasan and al-Ḥusayn — the mercy of Allah be upon them both and upon ʿAlī — read (وَأَرْجُلِكُمْ), and ʿAlī heard that while he was judging between people, and he said: ﴿وَأَرْجُلَكُمْ﴾ — this is of what is placed earlier and later in speech.
And Abū Isḥāq narrated from al-Ḥārith from ʿAlī, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: Wash the feet, i.e. (up to) the ankles. And likewise it is narrated from Ibn Masʿūd and Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah have mercy on them both, that they read ﴿وأرجَلَكُمْ﴾ in the accusative.
And al-kaʿb is the bone protruding at the end of the shin by the foot; and every joint is a kaʿb according to the Arabs, but there was no need to say "the kaʿb whose description is such-and-such," because it is evident and clear.
* And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿أَوْ جَآءَ أَحَدٌ مِّنْكُمْ مِّنَ ٱلْغَائِطِ﴾ is a euphemism (kināya).
And al-ghāʾiṭ originally is a low-lying piece of ground.
Then He, exalted be His mention, said: ﴿أَوْ لاَمَسْتُمُ ٱلنِّسَآءَ﴾.
Concerning its meaning there are two views:
One of them was narrated by ʿAbīda from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, that he said: "The kiss is a form of touching, and everything short of intercourse is touching"; and Ibn ʿUmar said likewise.
And Muḥammad ibn Yazīd inclines to this view; he said: because He has already mentioned at the beginning of this surah what is required of one who has had intercourse, in His saying ﴿وَإِن كُنتُمْ جُنُباً فَٱطَّهَّرُواْ﴾. [Translator's note: the text has «ين يزيد» for «بن يزيد»; read as Muḥammad ibn Yazīd (al-Mubarrad).]
And ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās said: al-lams, al-mass and al-ghashayān (touching, contact, covering) are intercourse, but He, Majestic and Mighty, used a euphemism.
And Mujāhid said concerning the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿وَإذَا مَرُّوا بِاللَّغْوِ مَرُّوا كِرَامَاً﴾;
he said: When they mention sexual relations, they speak of it by euphemism.
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿فَتَيَمَّمُواْ صَعِيداً طَيِّباً﴾,
i.e. so head for (it).
And al-ṣaʿīd is the surface of the earth.
Ibn ʿAbbās said: The best ṣaʿīd is tilled soil.
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿مَا يُرِيدُ ٱللَّهُ لِيَجْعَلَ عَلَيْكُم مِّنْ حَرَجٍ﴾.
Mujāhid said: That is, of narrowness.
* Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿وَلَـٰكِن يُرِيدُ لِيُطَهِّرَكُمْ﴾.
And Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab read ﴿لِيُطْهِرَكم﴾, and the meaning is the same, just as one says نَجَّاه and أَنْجَاه (he saved him).

nahhas-meani:7-7.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَٱذْكُرُواْ نِعْمَةَ ٱللَّهِ عَلَيْكُمْ وَمِيثَاقَهُ ٱلَّذِي وَاثَقَكُم بِهِ﴾.
The position of Ibn ʿAbbās is that he said: (It is) the covenant which He made with the believers among the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ: to hear and obey in what they liked and what they disliked.
Mujāhid said: (It is) the covenant which He took from the children of Adam, meaning His saying: ﴿وَإِذْ أَخَذَ رَبُّكَ مِنْ بَنِي آدَمَ مِنْ ظُهُورِهِمْ ذُرِّيَّتَهُمْ﴾.

nahhas-meani:8-8.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿يَا أَيُّهَآ ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ كُونُواْ قَوَّامِينَ للَّهِ شُهَدَآءَ بِٱلْقِسْطِ﴾.
القسط is justice.
* Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿وَلاَ يَجْرِمَنَّكُمْ شَنَآنُ قَوْمٍ﴾.
That is, let it not drive you; and we have explained it above.
And it has been read ﴿ولا يُجْرِمنَّكم﴾.
Al-Kisāʾī said: They are two dialectal forms.
And Abū Jaʿfar said: Abū Isḥāq said: The meaning of ﴿لا يَجْرِمنَّكُمْ﴾ is: let it not bring you into crime, just as you say:
آثَمني, i.e. he brought me into sin.
And الشنآن is hatred.

nahhas-meani:11-11.t:
And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿يَا أَيُّهَآ ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ ٱذْكُرُواْ نِعْمَتَ ٱللَّهِ عَلَيْكُمْ إِذْ هَمَّ قَوْمٌ أَن يَبْسُطُواْ إِلَيْكُمْ أَيْدِيَهُمْ فَكَفَّ أَيْدِيَهُمْ عَنكُمْ﴾.
Mujāhid said: "This is about the Jews: the Prophet ﷺ came to them seeking their help with a blood-money payment, and they resolved to kill him, but Allah, Majestic and Mighty, protected him from them."
And it is narrated from al-Ḥasan that he said: This was revealed about a man among the enemies of the Prophet ﷺ in one of his campaigns; he (the Prophet) faced the qibla to pray the prayer of fear, and this man came to kill him, but Allah prevented him from (harming) him.

nahhas-meani:12-12.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَبَعَثْنَا مِنهُمُ ٱثْنَيْ عَشَرَ نَقِيباً﴾.
النقيب in the language is the trustworthy one who knows the inner ways of the people, as if he knows what he investigates (yunaqqibu) of their affairs.
And Saʿīd narrated from Qatāda, who said: ﴿وَبَعَثْنَا مِنهُمُ ٱثْنَيْ عَشَرَ نَقِيباً﴾: from every tribe (sibṭ) a man as a witness over his tribe; ﴿وَقَالَ ٱللَّهُ إِنِّي مَعَكُمْ لَئِنْ أَقَمْتُمُ ٱلصَّلاَةَ﴾ to the end of the story.
* And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَآمَنتُمْ بِرُسُلِي وَعَزَّرْتُمُوهُمْ﴾.
Abū ʿUbayd said: ﴿عَزَّرْتُمُوهُمْ﴾: you honoured them.
And Yūnus said: You praised it. [Translator's note: the text has «عليها» (it, fem.), where «عليهم» (them) would be expected.]
And better than these two views is the view of Ibn Abī Najīḥ from Mujāhid, that the meaning of ﴿عَزَّرْتُمُوهُمْ﴾ is "you supported them," honouring being included in support.
And the evidence for this is His saying, the Exalted: ﴿وَتُعَزِّرُوهُ وَتُوَقِّروُهُ﴾.
And the basic sense of al-taʿzīr in the language is prevention; from it is "عزَّرتُ فلاناً," i.e. I inflicted on him that on account of which he refrains from repeating (the offence), just as you say "نكَّلتُ به," i.e. I inflicted on him what deters him from returning (to it).
And it is narrated from Saʿd that he said: "I saw myself the seventh of seven with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, having nothing (to eat) but the fruit of the ḥubla and samur trees; and then the Banū Asad came to be تعزِّرني concerning Islam," i.e. to discipline me.
And it goes back to what preceded, i.e. they would prevent me from what I am upon.

nahhas-meani:13-13.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿فَبِمَا نَقْضِهِم مِّيثَاقَهُمْ لَعنَّاهُمْ وَجَعَلْنَا قُلُوبَهُمْ قَاسِيَةً﴾.
And it is read "قَسِيَّةً".
And القاسية is (like this) as you say عَلِيَّةٌ and عَالِيةٌ, عَلِيٌّ and عالٍ, with one meaning.
And the other view: the meaning of "قَسِيَّة" is "not pure in faith," i.e. there is hypocrisy in them.
Abū Jaʿfar said: And this is a good view, because one says "درهمٌ قسِيٌ" (a counterfeit dirham) when it is adulterated with copper or something else.
Abū Jaʿfar said: And the most fitting (view) concerning it is that "قسَّية" is in the sense of قاسية, like زكيَّة and زاكية, except that faʿīla is more intensive than fāʿila; so the meaning is: We made their hearts hard, recoiling from faith and from success in obeying Me; because the people were not described as having anything of faith, such that their hearts could be described (as adulterated), in that their faith was mixed with disbelief, like counterfeit dirhams mixed with adulteration. [Translator's note: the text writes «قسَّية» here with a shadda on the sīn, as written.]
* Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿يُحَرِّفُونَ ٱلْكَلِمَ عَن مَّوَاضِعِهِ﴾.
It is possible that its meaning is: they alter its letters.
And it is possible that its meaning is: they take it in other than its meaning.
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَلاَ تَزَالُ تَطَّلِعُ عَلَىٰ خَآئِنَةٍ مِّنْهُمْ﴾.
Concerning it there are two views:
One of them was stated by Qatāda; he said: upon treachery.
And this is permissible in the language, being like their saying "قائلة" in the sense of qaylūla (midday nap).
And the other view was stated by Ibn Abī Najīḥ from Mujāhid: that by this the Jews who resolved to kill the Prophet ﷺ are meant; so the implied construction (taqdīr) according to this view is "upon a treacherous group," then (the adjective) was put in place of the thing qualified.

nahhas-meani:14-14.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿فَنَسُواْ حَظّاً مِّمَّا ذُكِرُواْ بِهِ﴾.
That is, they abandoned; and from it is (نَسُوا اللَّهَ فَنَسِيهُم), i.e. He abandoned them.
* Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿فَأَغْرَيْنَا بَيْنَهُمُ ٱلْعَدَاوَةَ وَٱلْبَغْضَآءَ إِلَىٰ يَوْمِ ٱلْقِيَامَةِ﴾.
And the meaning of "أَغْرَيْنَا" in the language is: We made (it) stick; and from it al-ghirāʾ (glue) is so called, for that with which things are stuck together.
Ibn Abī Najīḥ said: It means the Jews and the Christians.
And al-Rabīʿ ibn Anas said: By it He means the Christians specifically: "I stirred up enmity and hatred among them," i.e. as a requital for their disbelief; so they split into sects, among them the Nestorians, the Jacobites and the Melkites, each sect hostile to the other.

nahhas-meani:15-15.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿يَا أَهْلَ ٱلْكِتَابِ قَدْ جَآءَكُمْ رَسُولُنَا يُبَيِّنُ لَكُمْ كَثِيراً مِّمَّا كُنْتُمْ تُخْفُونَ مِنَ ٱلْكِتَابِ﴾.
It is narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās that he said: "A man of the Jews committed adultery, and they came seeking a ruling from the Prophet ﷺ in order to avert stoning from him, while stoning was (prescribed) for them in the Torah; and the Prophet ﷺ was informed of that."
* Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿قَدْ جَآءَكُمْ مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ نُورٌ﴾.
It was said that by "نورٌ" (a light) He means the Prophet ﷺ.
And it is a figurative representation (tamthīl), because light is that by which things become clear.

nahhas-meani:16-16.t:
Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿يَهْدِي بِهِ ٱللَّهُ مَنِ ٱتَّبَعَ رِضْوَانَهُ سُبُلَ ٱلسَّلاَمِ﴾.
السبل are the ways; and السلام admits two meanings:
One of them: that السَّلام is in the sense of السَّلامة (safety), just as one says اللَّذَاذ and اللَّذَاذة (pleasure).
And the other meaning: that al-Salām is one of the names of Allah, Majestic and Mighty.
So the meaning according to this is: by it Allah guides to His ways, i.e. whoever follows them, He saves him.

nahhas-meani:19-19.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿يَا أَهْلَ ٱلْكِتَابِ قَدْ جَآءَكُمْ رَسُولُنَا يُبَيِّنُ لَكُمْ عَلَىٰ فَتْرَةٍ مَّنَ ٱلرُّسُلِ﴾.
Qatāda said: He means Muḥammad ﷺ.
He said: And it has reached us that the interval (fatra) between Jesus and Muḥammad, Allah's blessings and peace be upon them both, was six hundred years.
And the meaning according to the lexicographers is: after a cessation of messengers, because the messengers came in succession between Moses and Jesus, Allah's blessings be upon them both; then that ceased until the Prophet ﷺ was sent.
* Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿أَن تَقُولُواْ مَا جَآءَنَا مِن بَشِيرٍ وَلاَ نَذِيرٍ﴾.
The Kufans said: The meaning is "lest you say" (an lā taqūlū); then "لا" was omitted, as He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿يُبَيِّنُ اللَّهُ لَكُمْ أَنْ تَضِلُّوا﴾.
And omitting "لا" is not permissible according to the Basrans, because it indicates negation.
And the meaning according to them is: out of aversion that you should say (karāhata an taqūlū).

nahhas-meani:20-20.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَإِذْ قَالَ مُوسَىٰ لِقَوْمِهِ يَاقَوْمِ ٱذْكُرُواْ نِعْمَةَ ٱللَّهِ عَلَيْكُمْ إِذْ جَعَلَ فِيكُمْ أَنْبِيَآءَ وَجَعَلَكُمْ مُّلُوكاً﴾.
It is narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās that he said: He means the servant and the dwelling.
Qatāda said: No one before them had possessed a servant.
And al-Ḥakam ibn ʿUtayba, Mujāhid and ʿIkrima said: ﴿وَجَعَلَكُمْ مُّلُوكاً﴾: the dwelling, the servant and the wife.
And Zayd ibn Aslam said likewise, except that he said, in what is known from the Prophet ﷺ: "Whoever has a house — or he said, a dwelling — in which he takes shelter, and a wife, and a servant who serves him, is a king."
He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿وَآتَاكُمْ مَّا لَمْ يُؤْتِ أَحَداً مِّن ٱلْعَٱلَمِينَ﴾.
Mujāhid said: He means the manna and the quails, the parting of the sea, the gushing forth (of water) from the rock, and the shading by the clouds.

nahhas-meani:21-21.t:
Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿يَاقَوْمِ ادْخُلُوا الأَرْضَ المُقَدَّسَةَ الَّتِي كَتَبَ اللَّهُ لَكُمْ﴾.
Qatāda said: He means Syria (al-Shām).
And المقدَّسة in the language means the purified; and from it Bayt al-Maqdis (Jerusalem) was named,
i.e. the place in which one is purified from sins.

nahhas-meani:22-22.t:
Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿قَالُوا يَامُوسَىٰ إِنَّ فِيهَا قَوْماً جَبَّارِينَ﴾.
الجَبّار according to the lexicographers is the haughty one who resists abasement and subjugation.

nahhas-meani:23-23.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿قَالَ رَجُلاَنِ مِنَ ٱلَّذِينَ يَخَافُونَ أَنْعَمَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَيْهِمَا﴾.
It is narrated from Mujāhid that he said: The two men were of the twelve chiefs (nuqabāʾ) who were sent, and they were "Yūshaʿ ibn Nūn" and "Kalāb ibn Qāyinnā" — and it is also said: Yūqannā.
And al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: They were two believing men who were in the city of the tyrants.
And the evidence for this is that they said ﴿ٱدْخُلُواْ عَلَيْهِمُ ٱلْبَابَ، فَإِذَا دَخَلْتُمُوهُ فَإِنَّكُمْ غَالِبُونَ﴾, and we know that if they entered by that gate, victory would be theirs.
And Saʿīd ibn Jubayr read: ﴿مِنَ الَّذِينَ يُخَافُونَ﴾ with a ḍamma on the yāʾ.
He holds that the two of them were from among the tyrants, and that Allah favoured them with Islam.

nahhas-meani:24-24.t:
Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿قَالُواْ يَامُوسَىۤ إِنَّا لَنْ نَّدْخُلَهَآ أَبَداً مَّا دَامُواْ فِيهَا﴾.
That is, we do not accept counsel. So Allah informed the Prophet ﷺ that the People of the Book have never ceased disobeying the prophets, and that he has an example in that.
Abū ʿUbayda said: The meaning of ﴿فَٱذْهَبْ أَنتَ وَرَبُّكَ فَقَاتِلاۤ﴾ is: Go and fight, and let your Lord help you.

nahhas-meani:25-25.t:
Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿قَالَ رَبِّ إِنِّي لاۤ أَمْلِكُ إِلاَّ نَفْسِي وَأَخِي﴾.
And it is possible that the meaning is: and my brother has power over none but himself.
And it is possible that the meaning is: and I have power over my brother, because since he obeys him, he has command over (him) in obedience.
* Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿فَٱفْرُقْ بَيْنَنَا وَبَيْنَ ٱلْقَوْمِ ٱلْفَاسِقِينَ﴾.
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: The meaning is: So judge between us and the defiantly disobedient people.

nahhas-meani:26-26.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿قَالَ فَإِنَّهَا مُحَرَّمَةٌ عَلَيْهِمْ﴾.
That is, they are prevented from entering it.
And it is narrated that entering it was forbidden to them forever.
So according to this, the complete stop is at His saying ﴿عَلَيْهِمْ [Translator's note: the closing bracket is missing in the source.]
* Then He, the Exalted, said: ﴿أَرْبَعِينَ سَنَةً يَتِيهُونَ فِي ٱلأَرْضِ﴾.
And some of the lexicographers held that the meaning is ﴿فَإنَّها مُحَرَّمَةٌ عَليْهِم أَرْبَعِينَ سَنَةً﴾,
then He began anew and said: ﴿يَتِيهُونَ فِي ٱلأَرْضِ﴾.
* Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿فَلاَ تَأْسَ عَلَى ٱلْقَوْمِ ٱلْفَاسِقِينَ﴾.
It is possible that this is an address to the Prophet ﷺ, i.e. so do not grieve over a people whose description is this.
And it is possible that the address is to Moses ﷺ.
One says: أَسِيَ، يَأْسَى، أَسَىً when he grieves; and one says: أَسَى الشيءَ يأسو أَسْوَاً, when you have mended it; and the meaning is that he removed that on account of which grief occurs. [Translator's note: the text vocalizes «الشيءُ» in the nominative; translated according to the sense.]
And "you have in so-and-so an iswa and an uswa (example)," i.e. when you see him to be like you, he shakes grief off you.

nahhas-meani:27-27.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَٱتْلُ عَلَيْهِمْ نَبَأَ ٱبْنَيْ ءَادَمَ بِٱلْحَقِّ﴾.
Mujāhid said: They were the two sons of Adam from his own loins, "Hābīl" and "Qābīl"; and among the signs that an offering of theirs had been accepted was that one of them would prostrate, then a fire would descend from the sky and consume the offering.
And القربان according to the lexicographers is (on the pattern) fuʿlān, from that by which one draws near (yutaqarrabu) to Allah, Majestic and Mighty.
And al-Ḥasan said: They were of the Children of Israel, because the offering existed among them.
Then He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿قَالَ لأَقْتُلَنَّكَ قَالَ إِنَّمَا يَتَقَبَّلُ ٱللَّهُ مِنَ ٱلْمُتَّقِينَ﴾.
The meaning: the one from whom (the offering) was not accepted said to the one from whom it was accepted: ﴿لأَقْتُلَنَّكَ﴾; then this was omitted because the hearer knows it.
And it is narrated that killing was forbidden at that time, just as it was forbidden when the Prophet ﷺ was in Mecca, and in the time of Jesus, upon him be peace; and for that reason he said: ﴿مَا أَنَا بِبَاسِط يَدِيَ إِلَيْكَ لأَِقْتُلَكَ، إِنِّي أَخَافُ اللَّهَ رَبَّ العَالَمِين﴾.

nahhas-meani:29-29.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿إِنِّيۤ أُرِيدُ أَن تَبُوءَ بِإِثْمِي وَإِثْمِكَ فَتَكُونَ مِنْ أَصْحَابِ ٱلنَّارِ﴾.
Al-Kisāʾī said: One says: بَاءَ بالشيءِ يبوُءُ به بَوْءً وبَوَاءً, when he goes back with it.
The Basrans said: One says بَاءَ بالشَّيْءِ when he acknowledges it, bears it and is bound by it.
And from it is "تبوأ فلانٌ الدَّارَ," i.e. he kept to the house and stayed in it.
One says: al-bawāʾ is equivalence, and "the killing is bawāʾ (an equal requital)"; and he recited:
فإن تكنِ القَتْلَى بَوَاءً، فإنكُمْ * فَتَىً مَّا قتَلْتُم آلَ عَوْفِ بنِ عَامِرِ
(If the slain are an equal requital, then — O family of ʿAwf ibn ʿĀmir — what a young man you have killed!)
"Abū al-ʿAbbās" Muḥammad ibn Yazīd said concerning His saying, the Exalted: ﴿إِنِّيۤ أُرِيدُ أَن تَبُوءَ بِإِثْمِي وَإِثْمِكَ﴾ — while he was a believer —: since the believer desires reward and does not stretch out his hand to him to kill, he was in the position of one who desires this.
And Abū al-Ḥasan ibn Kaysān was asked: How can a believer want his brother to sin and to enter the Fire?
He said: The wanting only occurred after he had stretched out his hand to kill.
So the meaning is: If you stretch out your hand to me to kill me, I will surely refrain from that, desiring the reward.
It was said to him: Then how did he say "with my sin and your sin," and what sin would be his if he were killed? He said: There are three aspects to it:
One of them: that you bear the sin of killing me and the sin of your (earlier) wrongdoing on account of which your offering was not accepted; and this aspect is narrated from Mujāhid.
And the other aspect: that you bear the sin of killing me and the sin of your aggression against me, because one may sin in aggression even if he does not kill.
And the third aspect: that had he stretched out his hand to him he would have sinned; so he considered that if he refrained from that, it would revert to his companion; and it became like your saying "The property is between him and Zayd," i.e. the property is between the two of them.
So the meaning is: that you bear our (joint) sin.
Abū Jaʿfar said: Among the most excellent of what is narrated about it, from Ibn Masʿūd and Ibn ʿAbbās, is that the meaning is: with the sin of killing me, and your sin in your previous acts of disobedience.
And if it is said: Is killing not an act of disobedience, so how could he want it? It is said: He did not say "that you bear my killing"; rather the meaning is "with the sin of killing me, if you kill me"; so he only wanted what is right.
* Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿وَذَلِكَ جَزَآءُ ٱلظَّالِمِينَ﴾.
It is possible that this is a report from Allah about the son of Adam, that he said this.
And it is possible that it is cut off from what precedes it.

nahhas-meani:30-30.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿فَطَوَّعَتْ لَهُ نَفْسُهُ قَتْلَ أَخِيهِ فَقَتَلَهُ﴾.
Qatāda said: That is, it made (it) seem fair.
And Mujāhid said: That is, it emboldened him, meaning that it assisted him in that.
And Abū al-ʿAbbās said: طوَّعَتْ is (on the pattern) faʿʿalat, from al-ṭawʿ and al-ṭawāʿiya, which is compliance with something.
* Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿فَأَصْبَحَ مِنَ ٱلْخَاسِرِينَ﴾.
That is, of those who lost their good deeds; and al-khusrān is diminution.

nahhas-meani:31-31.t:
Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿فَبَعَثَ ٱللَّهُ غُرَاباً يَبْحَثُ فِي ٱلأَرْضِ لِيُرِيَهُ كَيْفَ يُوَارِي سَوْءَةَ أَخِيهِ﴾.
Mujāhid said: Allah, Majestic and Mighty, sent two ravens, and they fought until one of them killed the other; then it dug and buried it. And this son of Adam was the first to kill.
And it is narrated "that no believer is killed until the Day of Resurrection but he (the son of Adam) bears a share of the sin of whoever killed him." [Translator's note: the referent of «عليه» is not specified in the text; the gloss "the son of Adam" is added for clarity.]

nahhas-meani:32-32.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿مِنْ أَجْلِ ذٰلِكَ كَتَبْنَا عَلَىٰ بَنِيۤ إِسْرَائِيلَ أَنَّهُ مَن قَتَلَ نَفْساً بِغَيْرِ نَفْسٍ أَوْ فَسَادٍ فِي ٱلأَرْضِ فَكَأَنَّمَا قَتَلَ ٱلنَّاسَ جَمِيعاً﴾.
And al-Ḥasan read: ﴿أَوْ فَسَادَاً فَي الأَرْضِ فَكَأَنَّمَا قَتَلَ النَّاسَ جَمِيعاً﴾.
And the meaning according to his reading is: or did (some) corruption.
And Ibn ʿAbbās said concerning His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿فَكَأَنَّمَا قَتَلَ ٱلنَّاسَ جَمِيعاً﴾: he has ruined himself, and become like one who killed all mankind, i.e. in deserving the punishment.
And the slain person is entitled to support and to the pursuit of vengeance against the killer from all the believers.
Ibn ʿAbbās said: Saving it (a soul) is that he does not kill a soul that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has made inviolable.
And Qatāda said: Allah made his case grave, and so attached this (degree) of sin to him.
And it was said: It is a figurative representation (tamthīl), i.e. all mankind are his adversaries.
And the meaning of ﴿أَوْ فَسَادٍ فِي ٱلأَرْضِ﴾ — his corruption — is warfare and making the roads unsafe.
And in the ḥadīth of Ḥammād ibn Zayd, from Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd, from Abū Umāma ibn Sahl ibn Ḥunayf, who said: I heard ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān, may Allah have mercy on him, say: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: "The blood of a Muslim man is not lawful except for one of three: adultery after iḥṣān (being married), disbelief after faith, or killing a soul without (right of retaliation for) a soul."
And the meaning of ﴿فَكَأَنَّمَا أَحْيَا النَّاسَ جَمِيعاً﴾ according to Qatāda's view is that he is given reward in proportion to that.
And it was said: Gratitude to him becomes obligatory on all mankind, so it is as if he had done a favour to them all; this is narrated from Makḥūl.
And the view of Ibn ʿAbbās is the most fitting and the soundest of them.

nahhas-meani:33-33.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Exalted: ﴿إِنَّمَا جَزَآءُ ٱلَّذِينَ يُحَارِبُونَ ٱللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ وَيَسْعَوْنَ فِي ٱلأَرْضِ فَسَاداً أَن يُقَتَّلُوۤاْ أَوْ يُصَلَّبُوۤاْ أَوْ تُقَطَّعَ أَيْدِيهِمْ وَأَرْجُلُهُم مِّنْ خِلافٍ﴾.
Al-Ḥasan said: The ruler has the choice: whichever of these things he wishes, he does. And likewise Ibn Abī Najīḥ narrated from ʿAṭāʾ; and it is the view of Mujāhid, Ibrāhīm and al-Ḍaḥḥāk; and it is good in terms of the language, because "أو" frequently occurs for choice (takhyīr).
And Abū Mijlaz said: The verse is in order (of gravity): whoever wages war and kills and takes property is crucified; whoever kills is killed; whoever takes property and does not kill has his hand and foot cut off on opposite sides; and whoever neither kills nor takes property is banished.
And this view was narrated by Ḥajjāj ibn Arṭāt from ʿAṭiyya from Ibn ʿAbbās likewise, except that he said at its beginning: "whoever wages war and kills and takes property has his hand and foot cut off on opposite sides, then is crucified"; whereas in the view of Abū Mijlaz nothing is mentioned before the crucifixion.
And the proponents of this view argued from a ḥadīth narrated by ʿUthmān, ʿĀʾisha and Ibn Masʿūd from the Prophet ﷺ that he said: "The blood of a Muslim man is not lawful except for one of three…" and he mentioned the ḥadīth. They said: So killing him is barred unless he kills; hence the verse must be (taken) according to ranks.
And al-Zuhrī said concerning His saying, the Exalted: ﴿أَوْ يُنفَوْاْ مِنَ ٱلأَرْضِ﴾: whenever it is known that he is in a place, he is fought until he leaves it.
And the people of Kufa said: Banishment (al-nafy) here is imprisonment.
And this is narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās with a weak chain of transmission.
And Saʿīd ibn Jubayr and ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz said: He is banished from his town to another town.
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿ذَٰلِكَ لَهُمْ خِزْيٌ فِي ٱلدُّنْيَا، وَلَهُمْ فِي ٱلآخِرَةِ عَذَابٌ عَظِيمٌ﴾.
One says: خَزِيَ يَخْزَى خِزْيَاً when he is disgraced and confounded; and خَزِي يخزَى خِزَايةً when he is ashamed, as though he were confounded out of aversion to doing what is shameful.

nahhas-meani:35-35.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ ٱتَّقُواْ ٱللَّهَ وَٱبْتَغُوۤاْ إِلَيهِ ٱلْوَسِيلَةَ﴾.
Ibn ʿAbbās said: He means nearness (al-qurba); and al-Ḥasan said likewise.
And Mūsā ibn Wardān narrated from Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Al-wasīla is a rank with Allah, Majestic and Mighty, above which there is no rank."

nahhas-meani:37-37.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿يُرِيدُونَ أَن يَخْرُجُواْ مِنَ ٱلنَّارِ وَمَا هُم بِخَارِجِينَ مِنْهَا﴾.
Yazīd al-Faqīr said: It was said to Jābir ibn ʿAbd Allāh: "You, O Companions of Muḥammad, say that some people will come out of the Fire, while Allah says ﴿وَمَا هُم بِخَارِجِينَ مِنْهَا﴾?" Jābir said: "You make the general specific and the specific general; this is only about the disbelievers specifically." So I read the verse from its beginning to its end, and behold, it was about the disbelievers specifically.

nahhas-meani:38-38.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَٱلسَّارِقُ وَٱلسَّارِقَةُ فَٱقْطَعُوۤاْ أَيْدِيَهُمَا﴾.
Sībawayh said: The meaning is: "And among what has been prescribed for you: the male thief and the female thief."
* Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿جَزَآءً بِمَا كَسَبَا نَكَالاً مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ﴾.
One says: نَكَّلْتُ بهِ, when you have done to him what should make him shrink back from that deed.

nahhas-meani:39-39.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿فَمَن تَابَ مِن بَعْدِ ظُلْمِهِ وَأَصْلَحَ فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَتُوبُ عَلَيْهِ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ غَفُورٌ رَّحِيمٌ﴾.
The meaning: Forgiving to him. And Allah made the repentance of disbelievers avert the prescribed punishments (ḥudūd) from them, because that is more conducive to (their entering) Islam; and He made the repentance of Muslims from theft and fornication not avert the prescribed punishments from them, because that is greater for their rewards in the Hereafter and a stronger deterrent to whoever is inclined to do the like of what they did.
And Mujāhid and al-Shaʿbī said: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd read: ﴿والسَّارِقُ وَالسَّارِقَةُ فَاقْطَعُوا أَيمْانَهُمَا﴾.

nahhas-meani:41-41.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿يٰأَيُّهَا ٱلرَّسُولُ لاَ يَحْزُنكَ ٱلَّذِينَ يُسَارِعُونَ فِي ٱلْكُفْرِ﴾.
That is, let not their hastening into disbelief grieve you, for Allah, Majestic and Mighty, has promised you victory.
* Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿مِنَ ٱلَّذِينَ قَالُوۤاْ آمَنَّا بِأَفْوَاهِهِمْ وَلَمْ تُؤْمِن قُلُوبُهُمْ﴾.
Mujāhid said: He means the hypocrites.
* Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿وَمِنَ ٱلَّذِينَ هَادُواْ سَمَّاعُونَ لِلْكَذِبِ﴾.
Mujāhid said: He means the Jews.
As for the meaning of ﴿سَمَّاعُونَ لِلْكَذِبِ﴾ — when a person hears both good and evil — there are two views concerning it:
One of them: that the meaning is "receptive to lies"; and this is well known in the language: one says "Do not listen to so-and-so," i.e. do not accept (what comes) from him; and from it is "سمعَ اللَّهُ لمن حَمِده" (Allah hears whoever praises Him), meaning He accepts, because Allah, Majestic and Mighty, hears everything.
And the other view: that they are avid listeners for the sake of lies, as you say "I honour so-and-so for you," i.e. for your sake.
* Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿سَمَّاعُونَ لِقَوْمٍ آخَرِينَ لَمْ يَأْتُوكَ﴾.
That is, they are spies for another people who have not come to you.
* Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿يُحَرِّفُونَ ٱلْكَلِمَ مِن بَعْدِ مَوَاضِعِهِ﴾.
That is, after Allah had put it in its places, making its lawful lawful and its forbidden forbidden.
* Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿يَقُولُونَ إِنْ أُوتِيتُمْ هَـٰذَا فَخُذُوهُ وَإِن لَّمْ تُؤْتَوْهُ فَٱحْذَرُواْ﴾.
That is, the Jews say: If you are given this distorted ruling, take it; and if you are not given it, beware of acting on it.
And the meaning of this is that a man of theirs committed adultery while he was muḥṣan (married), and stoning had been prescribed in the Torah for whoever commits adultery while muḥṣan; so some of them said: "Go to Muḥammad; perhaps he will give you a ruling other than stoning." So they came to the Prophet ﷺ, and he ordered stoning, after the Torah had been brought and the obligation of stoning was found in it, whereas they had denied that.
* Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿وَمَن يُرِدِ ٱللَّهُ فِتْنَتَهُ فَلَن تَمْلِكَ لَهُ مِنَ ٱللَّهِ شَيْئاً﴾.
It was said: The meaning of al-fitna here is testing.
And it was said: Its meaning is punishment.
* Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿أُوْلَـٰئِكَ ٱلَّذِينَ لَمْ يُرِدِ ٱللَّهُ أَن يُطَهِّرَ قُلُوبَهُمْ لَهُمْ فِي ٱلدُّنْيَا خِزْيٌ﴾.
That is, exposure and humiliation, when the Torah was brought and their lie became clear.
And it was said: Their disgrace in this world is the taking of the jizya, and humiliation.

nahhas-meani:42-42.t:
Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿سَمَّاعُونَ لِلْكَذِبِ أَكَّالُونَ لِلسُّحْتِ﴾.
Zirr narrated from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd that he said: Al-suḥt is bribery.
And Masrūq said: I asked ʿAbd Allāh about injustice in judgement. He said: That is disbelief. I said: Then what is al-suḥt? He said: That a man fulfils a need for his brother, and the latter gives him a gift, and he accepts it.
And al-suḥt in the speech of the Arabs is of various kinds, all united by its being what wipes out (yusḥitu) a person's religion; one says: سَحَته and أَسْحتَه, when he has eradicated it; and from it is:
وَعَضُّ زَمَانٍ يا ابنَ مَرْوَانَ لَمْ يَدَعْ * مِنَ المَالِ إِلاَّ مُسْحَتَاً أَوْ مُجَلَّف
(And the bite of a time, O son of Marwān, that left of wealth nothing but what was wiped out or stripped bare.)
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿فَإِن جَآءُوكَ فَٱحْكُمْ بَيْنَهُمْ أَوْ أَعْرِضْ عَنْهُمْ﴾.
