Concerning this there are two views:
One of them is narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās, that he said: It is abrogated; it was abrogated by ﴿وَأَنِ احْكُمْ بَيْنَهُم بِمَا أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ﴾; and Mujāhid and ʿIkrima said likewise.
Al-Shaʿbī said: If he wishes he judges, and if he wishes he does not judge; and Ibrāhīm said likewise.
And al-Ḥasan said: There is nothing abrogated in al-Māʾida.
And the preferred view among the people of reasoning is the first view, because it is the view of Ibn ʿAbbās; and His saying, Mighty and Majestic, ﴿وَأَنِ احْكُمْ بَيْنَهُم بِما أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ﴾ must either be abrogating this verse,
or its meaning is "and judge between them by what Allah has sent down, if you judge"; so he who judges between them has become correct by consensus.
And in the ḥadīth from the Prophet ﷺ there is what strengthens it:
It is narrated from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Murra from al-Barāʾ ibn ʿĀzib (that a Jew whose face had been blackened with charcoal was brought past the Prophet ﷺ, and he asked about his case, and it was said: He committed adultery while muḥṣan…), and he mentioned the ḥadīth, and said at its end: The Prophet ﷺ said: "I am the first to revive what they have let die of the command of Allah," and he gave the order concerning him, and he was stoned.
And what makes clear to you that this is the (correct) view is His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿يَا أَيُّها الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا كُونُوا قَوَّامِينَ لِلَّهِ شُهَدَاءَ بِالقِسْطِ﴾.
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿فَٱحْكُمْ بَيْنَهُمْ بِٱلْقِسْطِ﴾,
i.e. with justice.

nahhas-meani:44-44.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿إِنَّآ أَنزَلْنَا ٱلتَّوْرَاةَ فِيهَا هُدًى وَنُورٌ﴾.
That is, in it is the clarification of the matter of the Prophet ﷺ, and of what they came seeking a ruling about.
* Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿يَحْكُمُ بِهَا ٱلنَّبِيُّونَ ٱلَّذِينَ أَسْلَمُواْ لِلَّذِينَ هَادُواْ﴾.
It is possible that the meaning is: in it is guidance and light for those who are Jews, by which the prophets judge.
And it is possible that the meaning is: by it the prophets who submitted judge for those who are Jews and against them; then (the latter) was omitted.
And it has been said that "لهم" (for them) is in the sense of "عليهم" (against them); and the ḥadīth of the Prophet ﷺ concerning Barīra, when he said "Stipulate the walāʾ for them," was interpreted to mean "against them," because he ﷺ would not command her to do something not binding; and Allah, exalted be His mention, said: ﴿وَإنْ أَسَأْتُم فَلَها﴾.
And ﴿الَّذينَ أَسْلَمُوا﴾ here is a naʿt (adjective) carrying the sense of praise, like ﴿بسمِ اللَّهِ الرحمنِ الرحيمِ﴾.
* Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿وَٱلرَّبَّانِيُّونَ وَٱلأَحْبَارُ﴾.
Abū Razīn said: The rabbāniyyūn are the scholars, the wise.
And al-rabbānī according to the lexicographers means "master (rabb) of knowledge," i.e. possessor of knowledge; and the alif and nūn were brought for intensification.
And what strengthens this is that it is narrated that Ibn al-Ḥanafiyya — the mercy of Allah be upon him — said when Ibn ʿAbbās died: "The rabbānī of knowledge has died."
And Mujāhid said: The rabbāniyyūn are above the aḥbār; and the aḥbār are the scholars, because they embellish (yuḥabbirūn) a thing, and it is their breasts that are embellished. [Translator's note: the sentence «لأنهم يُحَبِّرون لشيء، وهو صدورهم مُحَبَّر» appears corrupt in the source; translated as closely as possible.]
And Ibn ʿAbbās said: The ink (ḥibr) with which one writes was called ḥibr because by it (the writing) is made fine, i.e. made exact.
And al-Thawrī said: I asked al-Farrāʾ why the ḥabr was called ḥabr. He said: The scholar is called ḥabr and ḥibr, and the meaning is "ink of a ḥibr"; then (the muḍāf) was omitted, as He, the Exalted, said: ﴿وَاسْألِ القَرْيَةَ﴾. Then I asked al-Aṣmaʿī, and he said: That is nothing; it was only called ḥabr because of its leaving a mark; one says "on his teeth is ḥabra," i.e. yellowness or blackness.
* Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿بِمَا ٱسْتُحْفِظُواْ مِن كِتَابِ ٱللَّهِ﴾.
That is, (what) they were entrusted with.
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَمَن لَّمْ يَحْكُم بِمَآ أَنزَلَ ٱللَّهُ فَأُوْلَـٰئِكَ هُمُ ٱلْكَافِرُونَ﴾.
Ibn ʿAbbās said: He is a disbeliever by it, but not with disbelief in Allah, His angels and His books.
And al-Shaʿbī said: The first is about the Muslims, the second about the Jews, and the third about the Christians.
And someone else said: Whoever rejects one of the rulings of Allah has disbelieved.
I say: And the jurists have agreed unanimously that whoever says that stoning is not obligatory upon one who commits adultery while muḥṣan is a disbeliever, because he has rejected one of the rulings of Allah, Majestic and Mighty.
And it is narrated that Ḥudhayfa was asked about these verses: Are they about the Children of Israel? He said: Yes, they are about them, and you will surely follow their path step by step (lit. sandal for sandal).
And al-Ḥasan said: Allah, Majestic and Mighty, took three things (as a covenant) from the judges:
that they not follow desire, that they not fear people but fear Him, and that they not sell His signs for a small price.
And the best of what has been said about this is what al-Aʿmash narrated from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Murra, from al-Barāʾ, who said: They are all about the disbelievers — meaning ﴿فَأُوْلَـٰئِكَ هُمُ ٱلْكَافِرُونَ﴾, ﴿فَأْولَئِكَ هُمُ الظَّالِمُون﴾ and ﴿فَأْولَئِكَ هُمُ الفَاسِقُون﴾.
[And the implied construction (taqdīr) according to this view is: "And those who did not judge by what Allah has sent down — those are the disbelievers."]

nahhas-meani:45-45.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿فَمَن تَصَدَّقَ بِهِ فَهُوَ كَفَّارَةٌ لَّهُ﴾.
Ibn ʿAbbās said: It is an expiation for the one who inflicted the wound; and ʿIkrima said likewise.
And the meaning: whoever gives up his right as charity.
And ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr said: It is an expiation for the wounded one, i.e. the like of that is expiated of his sins; and Ibn Masʿūd and Jābir ibn Zayd, may Allah have mercy on them both, said likewise.

nahhas-meani:48-48.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَمُهَيْمِناً عَلَيْهِ﴾.
Ibn ʿAbbās said: That is, entrusted with it.
And Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said: The Qurʾān is entrusted with the books that preceded it.
And Qatāda said: That is, a witness.
And Abū al-ʿAbbās Muḥammad ibn Yazīd said: The origin is muʾaymin ʿalayhi, i.e. trustworthy; then hāʾ was substituted for the hamza, just as one says هرمَتُ الماء and أرمتُ الماء (I poured out the water). [Translator's note: the forms are as written in the source; the usual pair is «هَرَقْتُ / أَرَقْتُ الماء».]
And Abū ʿUbayd said: One says هَيْمنَ على الشيء يهيمنُ, when he is its guardian.
And these views are all close in meaning, because if he is a guardian of the thing, he is entrusted with it and a witness (over it).
And Mujāhid and Ibn Muḥayṣin read ﴿ومُهَيْمَنَاً عَلَيهِ﴾ with a fatḥa on the (second) mīm.
And Mujāhid said: That is, Muḥammad ﷺ is entrusted with the Qurʾān.
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿لِكُلٍّ جَعَلْنَا مِنكُمْ شِرْعَةً وَمِنْهَاجاً﴾.
Ibn ʿAbbās said: A path and a way (sunna).
And Qatāda said: The religion is all one, and the laws differ.
And shirʿa and sharīʿa according to the lexicographers have one meaning, which is what is apparent and clear.
And from it: a road "of the shāriʿ," i.e. apparent and clear; and from it "هما في الأمرِ شَرَعٌ," i.e. their standing in the matter is equally apparent.
And al-minhāj in the language is the clear road.
And Abū al-ʿAbbās "Muḥammad ibn Yazīd" said: The sharīʿa is the beginning of the road, and the minhāj is the continuing road.
* And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَلَوْ شَآءَ ٱللَّهُ لَجَعَلَكُمْ أُمَّةً وَاحِدَةً﴾.
Ibn ʿAbbās said: Upon one religion.
* Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿وَلَـٰكِن لِّيَبْلُوَكُمْ فِي مَآ آتَاكُم﴾.
That is, to test you.

nahhas-meani:50-50.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿أَفَحُكْمَ ٱلْجَاهِلِيَّةِ يَبْغُونَ﴾.
It is narrated from al-Ḥasan, Qatāda, al-Aʿraj and al-Aʿmash that they read ﴿أَفَحَكَمُ الجَاهِليَّةِ يَبْغُونَ﴾.
Al-ḥakam and al-ḥākim (the judge) are the same in the language; it is as though they meant the soothsayer and the like among the judges of the Jāhiliyya; and this is in the reading of whoever reads "أَفَحَكَمُ". And the meaning of ﴿يَبْغُونَ﴾ is: they seek.
And Mujāhid said: By this the Jews are meant, and it refers to the matter of the two adulterers, when they brought them to the Prophet ﷺ imagining that he would pass a judgement on them other than stoning.
* Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿وَمَنْ أَحْسَنُ مِنَ ٱللَّهِ حُكْماً لِّقَوْمٍ يُوقِنُونَ﴾.
That is, whoever has certainty, it becomes clear to him that the judgement of Allah, Majestic and Mighty, is the truth.

nahhas-meani:51-51.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿يَـٰأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ لاَ تَتَّخِذُواْ ٱلْيَهُودَ وَٱلنَّصَارَىٰ أَوْلِيَآءَ﴾.
This is about the hypocrites, because they used to side with the polytheists and inform them of the secrets of the believers.

nahhas-meani:52-52.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿فَتَرَى ٱلَّذِينَ فِي قُلُوبِهِم مَّرَضٌ﴾,
i.e. hypocrisy, ﴿يُسَارِعُونَ فِيهِمْ﴾.
The meaning: they hasten to assist them; then (the muḍāf) was omitted, as He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿وَاسْأَلِ القَرَيَةَ﴾.
* Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿يَقُولُونَ نَخْشَىٰ أَن تُصِيبَنَا دَآئِرَةٌ﴾.
Concerning its meaning there are two views:
One of them is narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās; he said: They say: We fear that the matter will not last for Muḥammad.
And the other view: We fear that a drought will strike us and they will not give us of their surplus.
And the first view is closer to the meaning, as though it is from دارت تدور (to turn), i.e. we fear that matters will turn.
And what indicates it is His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿فَعَسَى ٱللَّهُ أَن يَأْتِيَ بِٱلْفَتْحِ أَوْ أَمْرٍ مِّنْ عِندِهِ﴾, because al-fatḥ is victory.
Ibn ʿAbbās said: So Allah brought victory: the fighting men of Banū Qurayẓa were killed, their offspring were taken captive, and Banū al-Naḍīr were expelled.
And it was said that the meaning of ﴿أَوْ أَمْرٍ مِّنْ عِندِهِ﴾ is: by commanding the Prophet, upon him be peace, to make known the names of the hypocrites, ﴿فَيُصْبِحُواْ عَلَىٰ مَآ أَسَرُّواْ فِيۤ أَنْفُسِهِمْ نَادِمِينَ﴾.

nahhas-meani:53-53.t:
Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿وَيَقُولُ ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ أَهُـۤؤُلاۤءِ ٱلَّذِينَ أَقْسَمُواْ بِٱللَّهِ جَهْدَ أَيْمَانِهِمْ إِنَّهُمْ لَمَعَكُمْ﴾.
That is, are these the ones who exerted themselves in oaths that they would not take the polytheists as allies?
* Then He, the Exalted, said: ﴿حَبِطَتْ أَعْمَالُهُمْ﴾; and this is like His saying, the Exalted: ﴿الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا وَصَدُّوا عَنْ سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ أَضَلَّ أَعْمَالَهُم﴾.

nahhas-meani:54-54.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿يٰأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ مَن يَرْتَدَّ مِنكُمْ عَن دِينِهِ فَسَوْفَ يَأْتِي ٱللَّهُ بِقَوْمٍ يُحِبُّهُمْ وَيُحِبُّونَهُ﴾.
Concerning the meaning of this there are two views:
Al-Ḥasan said: By Allah, it is Abū Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, and his companions.
Abū Jaʿfar narrated to us; he said: al-Ḥasan ibn ʿUmar ibn Abī al-Aḥwaṣ al-Kūfī narrated to us; he said: Aḥmad ibn Yūnus narrated to us; (from) al-Sarī, meaning Ibn Yaḥyā, who said: Al-Ḥasan recited this verse: ﴿يٰأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ مَن يَرْتَدَّ مِنكُمْ عَن دِينِهِ فَسَوْفَ يَأْتِي ٱللَّهُ بِقَوْمٍ يُحِبُّهُمْ وَيُحِبُّونَهُ﴾ until he finished the verse, and al-Ḥasan said: So Allah — by Allah — entrusted it to Abū Bakr and his companions. [Translator's note: the isnad reads «أحمد بن يونس السري يعني ابن يحيى»; a connecting «عن» (from) appears to be missing before al-Sarī.]
And Shuʿba narrated from Simāk ibn Ḥarb, from ʿIyāḍ al-Ashʿarī, who said: When ﴿فَسَوْفَ يَأْتِي ٱللَّهُ بِقَوْمٍ يُحِبُّهُمْ وَيُحِبُّونَهُ﴾ was revealed, the Prophet ﷺ pointed to Abū Mūsā al-Ashʿarī, may Allah have mercy on him, and said: "They are the people of this man."
* Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿أَذِلَّةٍ عَلَى ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ أَعِزَّةٍ عَلَى ٱلْكَافِرِينَ﴾.
Abū Jaʿfar said: I heard Abū Isḥāq when he was asked about the meaning of this, and he said: He does not mean "أَذِلَّة" (lowly) in the sense of abasement; He only means that their side is gentle towards the believers and rough towards the disbelievers.
* Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿ذٰلِكَ فَضْلُ ٱللَّهِ يُؤْتِيهِ مَن يَشَآءُ﴾.
That is, that gentleness towards the believers and severity towards the disbelievers is a bounty from Allah, Majestic and Mighty, which He granted them.
[Translator's note: the entry announces two views but the second is not explicitly labelled; the Abū Mūsā report appears to represent it.]

nahhas-meani:55-55.t:
And His saying, blessed be His name: ﴿إِنَّمَا وَلِيُّكُمُ ٱللَّهُ وَرَسُولُهُ وَٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ﴾.
Abū ʿUbayd said: Hushaym and Yazīd informed us, from ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Sulaymān, from Abū Jaʿfar Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī, concerning His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿إِنَّمَا وَلِيُّكُمُ ٱللَّهُ وَرَسُولُهُ وَٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ﴾; he said: It means the believers. I said to him: It has reached us that it was revealed about ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, may Allah be pleased with him. He said: ʿAlī is one of the believers.
Abū ʿUbayd said: And this makes clear to you the saying of the Prophet ﷺ: "Whoever I am his mawlā, ʿAlī is his mawlā"; for mawlā and walī are the same; and the evidence for this is His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿اللَّهُ وَلِيُّ الَّّذِينَ آمَنُوا يُخْرِجُهُم مِنَ الظُّلمَاتِ إلَى النوُّرِ﴾,
then He said in another place: ﴿ذَلِكَ بِأَنَّ اللَّهَ مَوْلَى الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَأَنَّ الكَافِرينَ لا مَولَى لَهُمْ﴾.
So the meaning of the ḥadīth of the Prophet ﷺ concerns the allegiance (walāya) of religion, which is the most exalted of allegiances.
And someone other than Abū ʿUbayd said: (It means) whoever I am his helper, ʿAlī is his helper.

nahhas-meani:57-57.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿يَـٰأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ لاَ تَتَّخِذُواْ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱتَّخَذُواْ دِينَكُمْ هُزُواً وَلَعِباً مِّنَ ٱلَّذِينَ أُوتُواْ ٱلْكِتَابَ مِن قَبْلِكُمْ وَٱلْكُفَّارَ أَوْلِيَآءَ﴾.
And al-Kisāʾī read: (وَالكُفَّارِ أَوْلَيَاءَ).
And the meaning: from those who were given the Book, and from the disbelievers.
Al-Kisāʾī said: In the codex (ḥarf) of "Ubayy," may Allah have mercy on him: "ومنَ الكفَّارِ".
And it is narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah have mercy on him, that some of the Jews and the polytheists laughed at the Muslims at the time of their prostration, so Allah, the Exalted, revealed ﴿يَـٰأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ لاَ تَتَّخِذُواْ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱتَّخَذُواْ دِينَكُمْ هُزُواً وَلَعِباً﴾ to the end of the verses.

nahhas-meani:60-60.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿قُلْ هَلْ أُنَبِّئُكُمْ بِشَرٍّ مِّن ذٰلِكَ مَثُوبَةً عِندَ ٱللَّهِ﴾.
Concerning this there are two views:
It is narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās that he said: The Jews said of the community of Muḥammad ﷺ: "They are the people with the smallest share in this world and the Hereafter"; so Allah, Majestic and Mighty, revealed ﴿قُلْ هَلْ أُنَبِّئُكُمْ بِشَرٍّ مِّن ذٰلِكَ﴾, the verse.
And the other view — and it is the well-known, sound one — is that the meaning is: "Say: Shall I inform you of what is worse in recompense than your resentment against us?" because before it is ﴿هَلْ تَنْقِمُونَ مِنَّا إِلاَّ أَنْ آمَنَّا بِاللَّهِ﴾.
Al-Kisāʾī said: One says نَقَمْتُ على الرجل أَنْقِمُ نُقُومَاً ونِقْمَةً.
And نَقِمْتُ أَنْقَمُ has also been reported: when you dislike a thing with the most intense dislike.
* Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿مَن لَّعَنَهُ ٱللَّهُ وَغَضِبَ عَلَيْهِ وَجَعَلَ مِنْهُمُ ٱلْقِرَدَةَ وَٱلْخَنَازِيرَ﴾.
Mujāhid said: He means the Jews; (it was) a transformation (maskh) among them.
* Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿وَعَبَدَ ٱلطَّاغُوتَ﴾; and this is the reading of the people of Medina, Abū ʿAmr and al-Kisāʾī.
And Abū Jaʿfar read (وَعُبِدَ), like ضُرِبَ (passive), and there is no (valid) aspect for this.
And it is narrated from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd that he read: ﴿وَعَبَدوُا الطَّاغُوتَ﴾.
And it is narrated from Ubayy ibn Kaʿb, and from Abū Masʿūd by another route, that they read ﴿وَعَبَدَتِ الطَّاغُوتَ﴾.
And Ibn ʿAbbās read: ﴿وَعُبَّدُ الطَّاعوتِ﴾. [Translator's note: «الطَّاعوتِ» with ʿayn is as written; read «الطَّاغوتِ».]
And it is narrated from [ʿIkrima from Ibn ʿAbbās that "وعَابِد الطاغوت" is permissible; and it is narrated from] al-Aʿmash and Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb: ﴿وَعُبُدُ الطَّاغُوتِ﴾.
And Abū Wāqid al-Aʿrābī read: ﴿وعُبَّادُ الطَّاغُوتِ﴾.
And Ḥamza read: ﴿وَعَبُدَ الطَّاغُوتِ﴾.
So whoever reads ﴿وَعَبَدَ الطَّاغُوتَ﴾, the meaning for him is: "whomever Allah has cursed, and whoever worshipped ṭāghūt (false deities)";
and he construed the verb according to the form (lafẓ) of "مَنْ".
And whoever reads ﴿وَعَبَدوُا الطَّاغُوت﴾, for him it has that meaning, except that he construed it according to the sense of "مَنْ", as He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿وَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ يَسْتَمِعُونَ إِلَيْكَ﴾.
And whoever reads ﴿وَعَبَدَتِ الطَّاغُوتَ﴾ construed it as the feminine of the group, as He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿قَالَتِ الأَعْرابُ﴾.
And whoever reads ﴿وعُبَّدَ الطَّاغُوت﴾, for him it is the plural of ʿābid, as one says shāhid and shuhhad, ghāʾib and ghuyyab.
And whoever reads ﴿وَعَابِد﴾, for him it is a singular that conveys a group.
And whoever reads (وُعُبُد), for him it is the plural of ʿibād or ʿabīd, as one says mithāl and muthul, raghīf and rughuf.
And some of the grammarians said: It is the plural of ʿabd, as one says rahn and ruhun, saqf and suquf.
And whoever reads (وَعُبَّاد), it is the plural of ʿābid, as one says ʿāmil and ʿummāl.
And whoever reads (وَعُبُدَ الطَّاغُوتِ), most of the lexicographers hold that it is a solecism (laḥn); but it is permissible by a stratagem, namely that "عَبُد" is made a singular indicating a group, as one says "a man who is ḥadhur (wary), faṭun (astute), nadus (perceptive)"; so the meaning would be "and the servant of ṭāghūt"; and on this basis this reading is interpreted. [Translator's note: the vocalization «وَعُبُدَ» here, as opposed to Ḥamza's «وَعَبُدَ» above, is as written; the discussion of the pattern faʿul suggests «وَعَبُدَ» is meant.]
One says: عَبَدَهُ يَعبُدُه, when he has humbled himself to him with the utmost humility; and from it is "a بعير معبَّد," i.e. a camel made tractable with tar; and from it "a طريق معبَّد" (a beaten road); and from it one says: عَبِدْتُ أَعْبَدُ when I disdain, as he said:
* "وَأَعْبَدُ أَنْ تُهْجَى تمِيمٌ بِدَارِمِ" *
(And I disdain that Tamīm should be satirised by (way of) Dārim.)
And the meaning according to this is: and the servant of ṭāghūt.
And it has been said: al-fard in the sense of al-fard; and al-Nābigha is recited: [Translator's note: the two words are identical as written; presumably a form such as «الفَرُد / الفَرِد» was intended to be compared with «الفَرْد».]
مِنْ وَحْشِ وَجْرَةَ مُوشِيٍّ أكَارِعُهُ * طَاوِي المَصِيرِ، كَسَيْفِ الصَّيْقَلِ الفَرِدِ
(One of the wild oxen of Wajra, its shanks streaked, its belly lean, like the burnished peerless sword of the polisher.)
And it is also narrated (with) al-farad.
And it was said: ṭāghūt here means Satan; and likewise it is narrated from Burayda al-Aslamī that he read ﴿وَعَابِدِ الشَّيْطَانِ﴾.
And some of the scholars permitted ﴿وَعَبَدَ الطَّاغُوتِ﴾ in the genitive, in the sense of ʿabada (worshippers), like kātib and kataba; and the hāʾ is dropped from the like of this in the genitive construct (iḍāfa).

nahhas-meani:61-61.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿وَإِذَا جَآءُوكُمْ قَالُوۤاْ آمَنَّا وَقَدْ دَّخَلُواْ بِٱلْكُفْرِ وَهُمْ قَدْ خَرَجُواْ بِهِ﴾.
That is, they did not benefit from anything of what they heard, so they went out with their disbelief.

nahhas-meani:63-63.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿لَوْلاَ يَنْهَاهُمُ ٱلرَّبَّانِيُّونَ وَٱلأَحْبَارُ﴾.
And Abū al-Jarrāḥ read: (لَوْلاَ ينهاهم الرِّبِّيُّونَ) [verse 63].
Mujāhid said: (الربَّانيُّونَ والأَحْبَارُ) are the scholars and the jurists; and the rabbāniyyūn are above the aḥbār.
Abū Jaʿfar said: And the ribbiyyūn are the multitudes; it is taken from al-ribba, and al-ribba is a multitude; so (a person) was ascribed to it and called ribbī, then it was pluralised and called ribbiyyūn.
Abū Jaʿfar said: And the meaning is: How evil is the deed that these rabbāniyyūn and aḥbār do in their failing to forbid these (people).
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: There is no verse in the Qurʾān more fearsome to me than it — that we do not forbid (wrong).
And in this verse there is a ruling regarding the duty of scholars in forbidding wrong.

nahhas-meani:64-64.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿وَقَالَتِ ٱلْيَهُودُ يَدُ ٱللَّهِ مَغْلُولَةٌ غُلَّتْ أَيْدِيهِمْ﴾.
Concerning this verse there are three views:
The best of them is what is narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās, that he said: The Jews said that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is miserly.
And the meaning according to the lexicographers is by way of figurative representation (tamthīl): i.e. they said, "He withholds from us and has not given us abundance," when they suffered drought; as He, the Exalted, said: ﴿ولا تَجْعَلْ يَدَكَ مَغْلُولَة إلى عُنُقِكَ﴾; so this is the counterpart of that, and Allah knows best.
And it was said: The hand here is favour (niʿma).
And it was said: This view is a mistake, because of His saying ﴿بَلْ يَدَاهُ مَبْسُوطَتَانِ﴾; for the favours of Allah, Majestic and Mighty, are too many to be counted, so how could it be "rather, His two favours are outspread"? [Translator's note: the text has «غلظ» (coarseness), evidently for «غلط» (mistake); translated by the sense.]
And one who argued on behalf of those who said they are two favours said that the meaning is the outward favour and the inward favour.
And the third view: that the meaning is "He will not punish us," i.e. (His hand is) shackled from punishing us.
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿وَأَلْقَيْنَا بَيْنَهُمُ ٱلْعَدَاوَةَ وَٱلْبَغْضَآءَ إِلَىٰ يَوْمِ ٱلْقِيَامَةِ﴾.
That is, He made their violence (be) among themselves, so they hate one another and are not in agreement; and they are the most hateful of Allah's creatures to people.
And Mujāhid said: They are the Jews and the Christians.
And what he said is good, and it would refer back to ﴿لا تَتَّخِذُوا اليَهُودَ والنَّصَارَى أَوْلِيَاء﴾.
* Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿كُلَّمَآ أَوْقَدُواْ نَاراً لِّلْحَرْبِ أَطْفَأَهَا ٱللَّهُ﴾.
This is a figurative representation (tamthīl): i.e. whenever they gathered together, Allah scattered their affair.
And Qatāda said: Allah, Majestic and Mighty, humiliated them for their acts of disobedience; when the Prophet ﷺ was sent, they were under the hands of the Magians.
* Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿وَيَسْعَوْنَ فِي ٱلأَرْضِ فَسَاداً﴾.
That is, they strive to nullify Islam.

nahhas-meani:66-66.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَلَوْ أَنَّهُمْ أَقَامُواْ ٱلتَّوْرَاةَ وَٱلإِنْجِيلَ﴾.
That is, if they had made manifest what is in them of the description of the Prophet ﷺ.
﴿وَمَآ أُنزِلَ إِلَيهِمْ مِّن رَّبِّهِمْ﴾: by it He means the Qurʾān, and Allah knows best.
* Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿لأَكَلُواْ مِن فَوْقِهِمْ وَمِن تَحْتِ أَرْجُلِهِم﴾.
This indicates that they were in drought.
And ﴿مِن فَوْقِهِمْ﴾, according to the view of Ibn ʿAbbās, Mujāhid and al-Suddī, means rain; and ﴿وَمِن تَحْتِ أَرْجُلِهِم﴾ means vegetation.
And it was said: It may be a figurative representation (tamthīl), i.e. We would have given them abundance, as one says:
"So-and-so is in good from the top of his head to his foot," i.e. good has enveloped him.
And the first is the view of the people of interpretation.

nahhas-meani:67-67.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿يَـۤأَيُّهَا ٱلرَّسُولُ بَلِّغْ مَآ أُنزِلَ إِلَيْكَ مِن رَّبِّكَ وَإِن لَّمْ تَفْعَلْ فَمَا بَلَّغْتَ رِسَالَتَهُ﴾.
Concerning its meaning there are two views:
One of them: Convey all that has been sent down to you. What strengthens this is that Masrūq narrated from ʿĀʾisha that she said: "Whoever tells you that Muḥammad ﷺ concealed anything of the revelation has lied, for Allah says: ﴿يَـۤأَيُّهَا ٱلرَّسُولُ بَلِّغْ مَآ أُنزِلَ إِلَيْكَ مِن رَّبِّكَ وَإِن لَّمْ تَفْعَلْ فَمَا بَلَّغْتَ رِسَالَتَهُ﴾."
And the other view — held by most of the lexicographers — is that the meaning is: Make manifest what has been sent down to you from your Lord, i.e. convey it openly.
And what indicates this is His saying, the Exalted: ﴿وَٱللَّهُ يَعْصِمُكَ مِنَ ٱلنَّاسِ﴾, i.e. He protects you from them, lest they reach you with harm.
(يعصمك) is derived from ʿiṣām al-qirba (the strap of the water-skin), which is what it is tied with.

nahhas-meani:68-68.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿ولَيَزِيْدَنَّ كثيراً منهم ما أُنْزِل إليك طغياناً وكُفْراً﴾.
That is, they disbelieve in it, and so increase in disbelief upon their disbelief.
* Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿فَلاَ تَأْسَ عَلَى ٱلْقَوْمِ ٱلْكَافِرِينَ﴾.
That is, so do not grieve over them.

nahhas-meani:69-69.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ وَٱلَّذِينَ هَادُواْ وَٱلصَّابِئُونَ وَٱلنَّصَارَىٰ﴾.
Concerning this there are two views:
One of them: that by "those who believed" here He means "the hypocrites."
And the implied construction (taqdīr) is: "Those who believed with their tongues"; and what indicates this is His saying, the Exalted: ﴿ولا يَحْزُنْكَ الَّذِينَ يُسَارِعُون في الكُفْرِ مِنَ الذينَ قالوا آمنَّا بأَفْواهِهم ولم تُؤْمِنْ قُلوبُهُم﴾.
Then He, majestic be His name, said: ﴿مَنْ آمَنَ بِٱللَّهِ﴾.
So the meaning according to this view is: whoever has realised faith in his heart.
And the other view: that the meaning of ﴿مَنْ آمَنَ بِٱللَّهِ﴾ is: whoever remains firm in his faith, as He, the Exalted, said: ﴿يا أيُّها الذين آمَنُوا آمِنُوا باللَّهِ ورَسُولِه﴾.

nahhas-meani:70-70.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿كُلَّمَا جَآءَهُمْ رَسُولٌ بِمَا لاَ تَهْوَىٰ أَنْفُسُهُمْ فَرِيقاً كَذَّبُواْ وَفَرِيقاً يَقْتُلُونَ﴾.
He said: The Jews and the Christians share in the denial, and the Jews alone are distinguished by the killing.
And among the messengers were those who came with laws, books and rulings, such as Muḥammad ﷺ, Moses and Jesus, and these are protected (from being killed).
And among them were those who came with enjoining right, forbidding wrong and holding fast to the religion, such as John (Yaḥyā) and Zechariah, upon them both be peace.

nahhas-meani:71-71.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿وَحَسِبُوۤاْ أَلاَّ تَكُونَ فِتْنَةٌ فَعَمُواْ وَصَمُّواْ﴾.
Al-Ḥasan said: By al-fitna He means affliction.
And someone else said: The meaning of ﴿فَعَمُواْ وَصَمُّواْ﴾ is a figurative representation (tamthīl): i.e. they did not act on what they heard, nor [benefit] from what they saw, so they are in the position of the blind and the deaf.
* Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿ثُمَّ تَابَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَيْهِمْ﴾.
That is, He sent Muḥammad ﷺ to inform them that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, would turn to them in forgiveness if they abandoned disbelief.
﴿ثُمَّ عَمُواْ وَصَمُّواْ﴾, i.e. after the proof had become clear.

nahhas-meani:72-72.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿لَقَدْ كَفَرَ ٱلَّذِينَ قَالُوۤاْ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ هُوَ ٱلْمَسِيحُ ٱبْنُ مَرْيَمَ﴾.
Ibrāhīm al-Nakhaʿī said: Al-Masīḥ means the truthful one (al-ṣiddīq).
Abū Jaʿfar said: And we have found the scholars to have six views on the interpretation of its meaning besides this:
It is narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās: He was called Masīḥ because he was flat-footed, with no hollow (in the sole of his foot).
And someone else narrated from him: He was only called Masīḥ because he would not wipe (yamsaḥu) with his hand anyone with an affliction but that he was cured, and would not place his hand on anything but that he was granted what he wished concerning it.
And Thaʿlab said: Because he used to traverse (yamsaḥu) the earth, i.e. cross it.
And it was said: Because of his wandering through the earth.
And it was said: Because he came out of his mother's womb anointed (mamsūḥ) with oil.
And Abū ʿUbayd said: I reckon that its origin in Hebrew is mashīḥā.
He said: As for their saying "al-Masīḥ al-Dajjāl," he was only called Masīḥ because one of his eyes is wiped out (mamsūḥ); so he is masīḥ in the sense of mamsūḥ, as one says qatīl in the sense of maqtūl (killed).

nahhas-meani:75-75.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَأُمُّهُ صِدِّيقَةٌ كَانَا يَأْكُلاَنِ ٱلطَّعَامَ﴾.
(صِدِّيقة) is from al-ṣidq (truthfulness); and "fiʿʿīl" in the speech of the Arabs is for intensiveness, as one says sikkīt (very taciturn).
And He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿وصَدَّقَتْ بِكَلِماتِ رَبِّها وكُتُبِه﴾.
And from this Abū Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, was called ṣiddīq.
And it is narrated that he was only called ṣiddīq because, when he was told that the Prophet ﷺ had been taken by night to Jerusalem, he said: "If he said it, then he has spoken the truth."
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿كَانَا يَأْكُلاَنِ ٱلطَّعَامَ﴾.
Concerning its meaning there are two views:
One of them: it is a euphemism (kināya) for relieving oneself, just as intercourse is spoken of euphemistically as "covering" (al-ghashayān) and the like.
And it was said: They used to take nourishment as all other people take nourishment; so how can one who lives only by eating food be a god?
* Then He, exalted be His mention, said: ﴿ٱنْظُرْ كَيْفَ نُبَيِّنُ لَهُمُ ٱلآيَاتِ ثُمَّ ٱنْظُرْ أَنَّىٰ يُؤْفَكُونَ﴾.
That is, We have made the signs clear to them and made the matter plain, so from where are they turned away?
One says: أَفَكَهُ يَأْفِكُه, when he has turned him away.

nahhas-meani:77-77.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿قُلْ يَـۤأَهْلَ ٱلْكِتَابِ لاَ تَغْلُواْ فِي دِينِكُمْ غَيْرَ ٱلْحَقِّ﴾.
Al-ghuluww is going beyond (bounds).
Abū ʿUbayd said: As the Khawārij did; excess led them to declare [the people of] sins to be disbelievers.
He said: And what makes this clear to you is the saying of the Prophet ﷺ about them: (They pass through the religion as the arrow passes through the game), and passing through (al-murūq) is excess itself, because the arrow goes beyond the game.
* Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿وَلاَ تَتَّبِعُوۤاْ أَهْوَآءَ قَوْمٍ قَدْ ضَلُّواْ مِن قَبْلُ، وَأَضَلُّواْ كَثِيراً، وَضَلُّواْ عَن سَوَآءِ ٱلسَّبِيلِ﴾.
Ibn Abī Najīḥ said, from Mujāhid: He means the Jews.
And someone else said: Because they followed their appetites, sought the continuation of their leadership, and preferred that over the truth.
And al-hawā (desire) in the Qurʾān is blameworthy; the Arabs only use it of evil; as for good, they use appetite (shahwa), intention (niyya) and love (maḥabba).
* Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿وَأَضَلُّواْ كَثِيراً﴾.
Ibn Abī Najīḥ said: He means the hypocrites.
And someone else said: They went astray by following them.
* Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿وَضَلُّواْ عَن سَوَآءِ ٱلسَّبِيلِ﴾,
i.e. its straight course.

nahhas-meani:78-78.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿لُعِنَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ مِن بَنِيۤ إِسْرَائِيلَ عَلَىٰ لِسَانِ دَاوُودَ وَعِيسَى ٱبْنِ مَرْيَمَ﴾.
Abū Mālik said: Those who were cursed by the tongue of David were transformed into apes, and those who were cursed by the tongue of Jesus ﷺ were transformed into swine.
And it is narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās that he said: Those who were cursed by the tongue of David were the people of the Sabbath, and those who were cursed by the tongue of Jesus were those who disbelieved after the table (al-māʾida) was sent down.
And it is narrated from the Prophet ﷺ that he said: "The first [deficiency] that befell the Children of Israel was that one of them would see his brother in disobedience and forbid him, then that would not prevent him the next day from being his companion in eating and drinking; so Allah struck the hearts of some of them against others, and revealed the Qurʾān concerning them: ﴿لُعِنَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ مِن بَنِيۤ إِسْرَائِيلَ عَلَىٰ لِسَانِ دَاوُودَ وَعِيسَى ٱبْنِ مَرْيَمَ ذٰلِكَ بِمَا عَصَوْا وَّكَانُواْ يَعْتَدُونَ﴾."
Then he ﷺ said: "No! By Him in whose hand is my soul, (not) until you take hold of the hands of the wrongdoer and bend him firmly to the truth."

nahhas-meani:80-80.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿تَرَىٰ كَثِيراً مِّنْهُمْ يَتَوَلَّوْنَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ﴾.
Mujāhid said: He means the hypocrites.

nahhas-meani:82-82.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿لَتَجِدَنَّ أَشَدَّ ٱلنَّاسِ عَدَاوَةً لِّلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ ٱلْيَهُودَ وَٱلَّذِينَ أَشْرَكُواْ وَلَتَجِدَنَّ أَقْرَبَهُمْ مَّوَدَّةً لِّلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ ٱلَّذِينَ قَالُوۤاْ إِنَّا نَصَارَىٰ﴾.
Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said: They were seventy men whom the Negus (al-Najāshī) sent, and they were the most eminent of those with him in learning and age; the Prophet ﷺ recited "Yā Sīn" to them, and they wept and said: "Our Lord, we have believed, so record us among the witnesses."
And Allah also revealed concerning them: ﴿الَّذِينَ آتَيْنَاهُمُ الكِتَابَ مِنْ قَبْلِهِ هُمْ بِهِ يُؤْمِنُون﴾ up to His saying ﴿أُولَئِكَ يُؤْتَوْنَ أَجْرَهُمْ مَرَّتَيْنِ﴾, to the end of the verse.
And it is narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās that he said: They were a people from Abyssinia who came to the Prophet ﷺ, and with them were monks from among the monks of Syria; they believed and did not go back.

nahhas-meani:83-83.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿فَٱكْتُبْنَا مَعَ ٱلشَّاهِدِينَ﴾.
Isrāʾīl narrated from Simāk, from ʿIkrima, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: He means the community of Muḥammad ﷺ; and what makes clear to you the soundness of this view is His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَكَذَلِكَ جَعَلْنَاكُمْ أُمَّةً وَسَطَاً لِتَكُونُوا شُهَدَاءَ عَلَى النَّاسِ﴾.

nahhas-meani:87-87.t:
And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿يٰأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ لاَ تُحَرِّمُواْ طَيِّبَاتِ مَآ أَحَلَّ ٱللَّهُ لَكُمْ﴾.
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: These were some of the Muslims who said: "We will cut off our private parts and wear haircloth."
And Qatāda said: It was revealed about a group of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, among them ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib and ʿUthmān ibn Maẓʿūn, who said: "We will castrate ourselves and become monks."
And Mujāhid said: It was revealed about ʿUthmān ibn Maẓʿūn, ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ and others;
they said: "We will become monks and wear haircloth."
* And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَلاَ تَعْتَدُوۤاْ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لاَ يُحِبُّ ٱلْمُعْتَدِينَ﴾.
Al-iʿtidāʾ in the language is going beyond what is one's own to what is not one's own.
Al-Ḥasan said: Its meaning is: that you not do what you have been forbidden.

nahhas-meani:89-89.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿لاَ يُؤَاخِذُكُمُ ٱللَّهُ بِٱللَّغْوِ فِيۤ أَيْمَانِكُمْ﴾.
Concerning it there are two views:
One of them: that it is a man's saying "No, by Allah" and "Yes, by Allah"; and this view is narrated from ʿĀʾisha.
Al-Shāfiʿī said: And that is in obstinate dispute, anger and haste.
And the other view: that a man swears about something that he believes to be as he swore, and then it turns out to be otherwise; this view is narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās and Abū Hurayra.
And al-laghw in the language is what is discarded; so oaths that have no reality to them are called laghw.
Al-Kisāʾī said: One says: لَغَا يَلْغُو لَغْواً, or لَغِي يَلْغَى لغاً.
* And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَلَـٰكِن يُؤَاخِذُكُم بِمَا عَقَّدتُّمُ ٱلأَيْمَانَ﴾.
Al-Kisāʾī said: The meaning of ﴿عَقَّدْتُمُ﴾ is: you made binding.
Ibn Jurayj said: I said to ʿAṭāʾ: What is the meaning of ﴿عَقَّدْتُمُ﴾? He said: (Saying) "By Allah, besides whom there is no god." [Translator's note: the text has «ابن جريح» for Ibn Jurayj and «لا إليه» for «لا إله»; translated by the sense.]
And Abū ʿAmr read: ﴿عَقِّدْتُمْ﴾; he said its meaning is: you affirmed (them) emphatically. [Translator's note: the vocalization «عَقِّدْتُمْ» is as written.]
And Nāfiʿ narrated that Ibn ʿUmar, when he broke an oath without having affirmed the oath emphatically, would feed ten poor persons, a mudd for each poor person; and when he had affirmed the oath emphatically, he would free a slave.
It was said to Nāfiʿ: What is the meaning of "affirmed the oath emphatically"? He said: That one swears about the thing repeatedly.
* And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿فَكَفَّارَتُهُ إِطْعَامُ عَشَرَةِ مَسَاكِينَ﴾.
The meaning: the expiation of his sin, i.e. that which covers over his sin.
Abū Jaʿfar said: And the hāʾ in ﴿فَكَفَّارَتُهُ﴾ refers back to (ما) in ﴿بِمَا عَقَّدتُّمُ ٱلأَيْمَانَ﴾.
And this is the position of al-Ḥasan and al-Shaʿbī, because the meaning according to them is: the expiation of what you have bound of them.
And it was said: The hāʾ refers back to al-laghw; and the first is more fitting.
* Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿مِنْ أَوْسَطِ مَا تُطْعِمُونَ أَهْلِيكُمْ﴾.
ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar said: ﴿مِنْ أَوْسَطِ مَا تُطْعِمُونَ أَهْلِيكُمْ﴾: bread and dates, and bread and oil;
and the best of what you feed them is bread and meat.
And al-Aswad said: The average of what you feed your families is bread and dates.
Abū Isḥāq said: This admits three meanings in the language:
It is possible that the meaning of ﴿مِنْ أَوْسَطِ مَا تُطْعِمُونَ أَهْلِيكُمْ﴾ is: of the most moderate of what you feed them;
He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿وَكَذَلِكَ جَعَلْنَاكُمْ أُمَّةً وَسَطَاً﴾, i.e. just.
And it may be in terms of value.
And it may be in terms of satiety.
And Saʿīd ibn Jubayr read: ﴿مِنْ أَوْسَطِ مَا تُطْعِمُونَ أَهْلِيكُمْ أَوْ كَإِسْوَتِهِمْ﴾, i.e. like the example (iswa) of your families.
And it is narrated that a man recited to Mujāhid ﴿أَوْ كَإِسْوَتِهِم﴾, and he said to him: Do not read it except as ﴿أَوْ كِسْوَتُهُمْ﴾; and he said: I consider that to be a garment.
And in the reading of ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ubayy ibn Kaʿb: ﴿فَمَنْ لَمْ يَجِدْ فَصِيَامُ ثَلاَثَةِ أَيَّامٍ مُتَتَابِعَاتٍ﴾. [Translator's note: as written; the reading «متتابعات» is usually attributed to ʿAbd Allāh (ibn Masʿūd) and Ubayy ibn Kaʿb, so «و» (and) may have dropped out.]
* Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿ذٰلِكَ كَفَّارَةُ أَيْمَانِكُمْ إِذَا حَلَفْتُمْ﴾.
That is, that is the expiation of the sin of your oaths when you swear and break them; then (this) was omitted.
Abū Jaʿfar said: And "Muḥammad ibn Jarīr" preferred, concerning "أوْسَط", that it be in the sense of "most moderate" in terms of smallness and largeness (of quantity); he said: The most moderate of the provisions of the well-off is two mudds, and that is its highest; and the most moderate of the provisions of the one in straitened means is one mudd, which is a quarter of a ṣāʿ; and "ما" is maṣdariyya. As for the clothing:
Al-Ḥasan, Ṭāwūs and ʿAṭāʾ said: A garment, a garment (each).
And Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab said: A cloak and a turban.
And Mujāhid said: Whatever clothes is sufficient.
And this is closer to the language: that it be whatever the name "clothing" applies to, of what amounts to a garment or more, because there is no disagreement that what is less than a garment is not permissible.

nahhas-meani:90-90.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿يَـۤأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ إِنَّمَا ٱلْخَمْرُ وَٱلْمَيْسِرُ وَٱلأَنصَابُ وَٱلأَزْلاَمُ رِجْسٌ مِّنْ عَمَلِ ٱلشَّيْطَانِ﴾.
Mūsā ibn ʿUqba narrated from Nāfiʿ from Ibn ʿUmar, who said: Al-maysir is gambling.
And ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿUmar said: Al-Qāsim ibn Muḥammad was asked about chess: Is it maysir? And about backgammon (al-nard): Is it maysir? He said: Everything that bars from the remembrance of Allah and from the prayer is maysir.
Abū ʿUbayd said: He interpreted (in light of) the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿وَيَصُدَّكُمْ عَنْ ذِكْرِ اللَّهِ وَعَنِ الصَّلاَةِ﴾.
And al-Aṣmaʿī claimed that al-maysir was specifically with slaughter-camels: they used to divide it into twenty-eight shares.
And Abū ʿAmr al-Shaybānī said: They used to divide it into ten shares, then cast the arrows and gamble over their portions. And this view does not contradict what preceded, because even if al-maysir was specifically with slaughter-camels, it is gambling;
then whatever gambling was like it was called maysir, just as khamr was (originally) for one particular thing, and then every intoxicant was called khamr because it occupies its position.
And we have mentioned "al-anṣāb and al-azlām" at the beginning of the surah.
And al-rijs is stench.
* Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿فَٱجْتَنِبُوهُ لَعَلَّكُمْ تُفْلِحُونَ﴾.
That is, be on a side other than its side.
And it is narrated that ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him, kept saying, "O Allah, make (the ruling on) wine clear to us," until ﴿فَهَلْ أَنْتُمْ مُنْتَهُونَ﴾ was revealed; then he said: "We have desisted."

nahhas-meani:93-93.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿لَيْسَ عَلَى ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ وَعَمِلُواْ ٱلصَّالِحَاتِ جُنَاحٌ فِيمَا طَعِمُوۤاْ إِذَا مَا ٱتَّقَواْ وَآمَنُواْ وَعَمِلُواْ الصَّالِحَاتِ﴾.
Ibn ʿAbbās and al-Barāʾ said: When wine was forbidden, the Muslims said: "O Messenger of Allah, what of our believing brothers who died while drinking it?" So Allah, Majestic and Mighty, revealed ﴿لَيْسَ عَلَى ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ وَعَمِلُواْ ٱلصَّالِحَاتِ جُنَاحٌ فِيمَا طَعِمُوۤاْ﴾ to the end of the verse.
And al-Zuhrī narrated from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿĀmir ibn Rabīʿa that when ʿUmar wanted to apply the prescribed punishment to "Qudāma ibn Maẓʿūn," Qudāma said: "You have no right to flog me; Allah, Majestic and Mighty, has said: ﴿لَيْسَ عَلَى ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ وَعَمِلُواْ ٱلصَّالِحَاتِ جُنَاحٌ فِيمَا طَعِمُوۤاْ﴾, the verse." ʿUmar said: "You have erred in interpretation; if you had certainty, you would avoid what Allah has forbidden you." Then he gave the order concerning him and he was flogged.
It was said: This is better than the first, because in it is ﴿إِذَا مَا ٱتَّقَواْ وَآمَنُواْ﴾, and "إذا" is not for the past; so the meaning according to this — and Allah knows best — is (that it is) for the believers before and after, in general.
And this too has been narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās.
Abū Jaʿfar said: It was said: ﴿إِذَا مَا ٱتَّقَواْ﴾ polytheism, ﴿وَآمَنُواْ﴾ and believed, ﴿ثُمَّ اتَّقَواْ وَآمَنُواْ﴾ increased in faith, ﴿ثُمَّ اتَّقَواْ﴾ minor sins out of caution, ﴿وَّأَحْسَنُواْ﴾ performed supererogatory acts. [Translator's note: the text has «تَنَقَّلُوا» (moved about), evidently for «تَنَفَّلُوا» (performed supererogatory acts); translated by the sense.]
And Muḥammad ibn Jarīr said: The first fearing is fearing by receiving the command of Allah with acceptance and assent, holding it as religion, and acting (on it).
And the second fearing is fearing by remaining firm in assent.
And the third is fearing by excellence (iḥsān) and drawing near through supererogatory acts.

nahhas-meani:94-94.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿يَـۤأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ لَيَبْلُوَنَّكُمُ ٱللَّهُ بِشَيْءٍ مِّنَ ٱلصَّيْدِ﴾.
The meaning: He will surely test (to distinguish) your obedience from your disobedience.
* Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿تَنَالُهُ أَيْدِيكُمْ وَرِمَاحُكُمْ﴾.
Mujāhid said: What "your hands reach" is eggs and chicks, and what spears reach is what is large.

nahhas-meani:95-95.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿لاَ تَقْتُلُواْ ٱلصَّيْدَ وَأَنْتُمْ حُرُمٌ﴾.
Sharīk narrated from Sālim, [from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr: ﴿يَـۤأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ لاَ تَقْتُلُواْ ٱلصَّيْدَ وَأَنْتُمْ حُرُمٌ﴾];
he said: Killing it is forbidden in this verse.
One of the scholars said: That is, since killing game was forbidden to the one in iḥrām, his killing it is not a ritual slaughter (tadhkiya).
* And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَمَن قَتَلَهُ مِنكُم مُّتَعَمِّداً﴾.
Most of the jurists hold that the compensation (jazāʾ) is due from him whether he did it deliberately or by mistake. [Translator's note: the text has «معتمداً» for «متعمداً» (deliberately).]
And they held that His saying, the Exalted, ﴿وَمَن قَتَلَهُ مِنكُم مُّتَعَمِّداً﴾ is referred to His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَمَنْ عَادَ فَيَنْتَقِمُ ٱللَّهُ مِنْهُ﴾.
And they argued for that that the Prophet ﷺ "was asked about the hyena and said: It is game," and he prescribed a ram for it if the one in iḥrām killed it, and did not say "deliberately" or "by mistake."
Al-Zuhrī said: In the case of a mistake it is (established by) the Sunna.
And some of the people of knowledge said: The compensation is only due from him if he killed it deliberately; and they argued from the apparent sense of the verse.
ʿAbd Allāh ibn Aḥmad narrated to us; ʿAbd al-Salām; Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā; Abū al-Walīd narrated to us; Abū ʿAwāna narrated to us, from Abū Bishr, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, concerning His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَمَن قَتَلَهُ مِنكُم مُّتَعَمِّداً﴾; he said: There is nothing due from him for a mistake; it is only for the deliberate act — meaning the game. [Translator's note: the isnad «عبدالله بن أحمد عبدالسلام محمد بن يحيى» lacks connecting words (e.g. «بن» / «قال: نا»); the names are given as they stand.]
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿فَجَزَآءٌ مِّثْلُ مَا قَتَلَ مِنَ ٱلنَّعَمِ﴾.
It was said: al-naʿam in the language is "camels, cattle and sheep/goats"; and if camels are on their own they are called naʿam, but if "cattle and sheep/goats" are on their own they are not called naʿam.
And al-Aʿmash read: ﴿فَجَزَاؤُهْ مِثْلُ مَا﴾; and the meaning is "then its compensation is due from him," then "مِثْل" was made a badal (substitute) of "جزاؤه".
* And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿أَوْ كَفَّارَةٌ طَعَامُ مَسَاكِينَ﴾.
"أو" here is for choice (takhyīr).
And concerning its meaning there are several views:
And it was said: The judge has the choice.
And it was said: The first is applied, then the next.
And the first view is better, because the one who killed the game is the one addressed, and because it is well known that "أو" is for choice. [Translator's note: as written, the first view — evidently that the one who killed the game has the choice — is not stated explicitly before «وقيل».]
And Ṭalḥa and al-Jaḥdarī read ﴿أَوْ عِدْلُ ذَلِكَ صِيَامَاً﴾, and a group of the lexicographers rejected it and said: al-ʿidl is a load.
And al-Kisāʾī said: al-ʿadl and al-ʿidl are two dialectal forms with one meaning.
And al-Farrāʾ said: The ʿadl of a thing is its equivalent from another kind, and its ʿidl is its equivalent from its own kind.
And the Basrans rejected this distinction and said: al-ʿadl and al-ʿidl are the equivalent, whether from the same kind or from another kind, without difference, just as al-mithl does not differ.
And in the ḥadīth: "Allah will not accept from him a ṣarf or an ʿadl"; al-ṣarf is repentance, and al-ʿadl is ransom; (this) is narrated from the Prophet ﷺ.
Abū Ḥātim said: And the view of whoever said that they are "the obligatory and the supererogatory" is not known; and what Abū Ḥātim rejected was said by al-Māzarī. [Translator's note: the text repeats «مَن» («whoever»); and «المازري» may stand for al-Māzinī; translated as written.]
* Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿لِّيَذُوقَ وَبَالَ أَمْرِهِ﴾.
That is, its severity; and from it is "طعامٌ وبيلٌ" (unwholesome food), when it is heavy; and from it is his saying:
* "عَقِيلَةُ شَيْخٍ كَالَوبِيلِ يَلَنْدَدِ" *
(The prized one of an old man like a heavy staff, fiercely quarrelsome.)
* Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿عَفَا ٱللَّهُ عَمَّا سَلَف وَمَنْ عَادَ فَيَنْتَقِمُ ٱللَّهُ مِنْهُ﴾.
ʿAṭāʾ said: Allah has pardoned what is past in the Jāhiliyya.
And Shurayḥ and Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said: Judgement is passed against him the first time; and if he does it again, judgement is not passed against him, and it is said to him: "Go; Allah will take retribution from you," i.e. your sin is too great to be expiated;
just as the false (perjurious) oath has no expiation according to most of the people of knowledge, because of the greatness of its sin.
I say: ʿAṭāʾ's view on this is more fitting; and the meaning is: whoever does it again after what is past in the Jāhiliyya, Allah will take retribution from him through things of punishment that befall him; or it is like His saying ﴿لِّيَذُوقَ وَبَالَ أَمْرِهِ﴾.
